jobs.title: Services Sales Manager
jobs.excerpt: At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges.  We challenge our limits.
jobs.description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

So, what’s the role all about?

Demand from the world’s leading financial institutions for Financial Crime and Compliance services is accelerating.

Actimize Professional Services is seeking a highly visible, commercially driven and proactive Principal, Strategic Services Sales to originate, shape and close large, strategic services engagements across EMEA.

Reporting to the Strategic Services Sales Leader, you will operate as a senior individual contributor within our established banking, financial services and insurance client base. This role sits within the team responsible for selling unattached services after the software license sale and does not cover services attached to a new license transaction.

While the role is focused on existing-account expansion, success depends on bringing a strong hunter mindset: proactively identifying whitespace and independently generating new business through cross-sell and upsell opportunities within Actimize customers.

Combining deep Financial Crime and Compliance knowledge, consulting credibility and strong commercial judgement, you will understand client pain points, architect differentiated solutions, mobilise the right Actimize stakeholders and convert complex opportunities into long-term client partnerships.

Business Unit

Actimize Professional Services

Reports to

Strategic Services Sales Leader

Location

London, United Kingdom

Scope

EMEA; senior individual contributor focused exclusively on unattached, post-license strategic services sales into existing customers

Domain

Financial Crime and Compliance, including AML and Fraud

The Services Portfolio

This role exclusively covers unattached services sold to Actimize customers following the software license sale. It does not include implementation or other services sold as part of, or attached to, a new license transaction.

The focus is on identifying whitespace, expanding existing engagements and creating new strategic services opportunities across:

  • Large-scale, multi-year transformational programmes in Financial Crime and Compliance
  • Transformational consulting and advisory
  • Business and technical managed services, including business-as-usual (BAU) engagements
  • Financial crime operations services

How will you make an impact?

Own account and territory growth planning.

Develop actionable services growth plans for priority EMEA accounts by analysing the installed base, identifying whitespace, mapping executive stakeholders and translating client priorities into focused opportunity plans.

Generate and shape demand.

Lead client workshops, executive briefings and value-discovery sessions that surface unmet needs, create urgency and shape new consulting, transformation and managed services opportunities independent of new license transactions.

Understand the client agenda.

Engage credibly with senior business, technology, operations and compliance stakeholders, speaking the language of financial institutions and translating their Financial Crime and Compliance challenges into clear service outcomes.

Architect complex, high-quality deals.

Construct large, strategic and often multi-year services propositions, defining the value case, scope, delivery model, commercial structure, pricing and roadmap while maintaining accountability for margin, delivery risk and overall deal quality.

Lead pursuits to closure.

Own the end-to-end sales cycle for complex services deals, from early discovery and qualification through proposal, negotiation and signature, maintaining momentum and executive alignment throughout.

Partner with the regional sales organisation.

Work alongside account executives and regional sales leaders on aligned account strategies: account teams retain ownership of the overall client relationship and software agenda, while this role leads the origination, shaping and closure of unattached post-license services opportunities, with shared executive engagement and coordinated account governance.

Expand existing relationships and engagements.

Develop durable relationships with client executives, uncover adjacent needs and extend the value and scope of current engagements by positioning Actimize as a trusted strategic services partner.

Develop thought leadership and repeatable propositions.

Bring relevant market, regulatory and operating-model insights to clients and work with consulting, product and delivery teams to create differentiated, repeatable services propositions that respond to common client needs.

Mobilise Actimize.

Build trust with internal leaders across Professional Services, software sales, product, pre-sales, delivery, legal, finance and partners to secure the expertise and sponsorship required to shape and position winning deals.

Maintain post-sale continuity.

Remain engaged through mobilisation and key executive checkpoints to ensure the value proposition sold is translated into measurable client outcomes, delivery risks are surfaced early and future expansion opportunities are identified.

Drive commercial discipline.

Maintain a high-quality pipeline and accurate forecast, apply rigorous qualification and opportunity governance, and make sound decisions on competitive strategy, commercials, margin, contractual position and delivery risk.

Create market impact.

Establish a visible presence quickly, independently build a point of view on priority accounts, and translate strategic insight into practical opportunity plans that strengthen Actimize’s position as a Financial Crime and Compliance services partner.

Have you got what it takes?

Experience and Capabilities

  • Typically 8–15 years of relevant experience, including proven success independently originating and selling complex, high-value consulting-led, transformation or managed services engagements into existing large financial-institution customers outside a new software license sale. Equivalent depth of experience and demonstrated capability will also be considered.

  • Strong knowledge of Financial Crime and Compliance, including the priorities and pain points facing financial institutions across areas such as AML, fraud, sanctions, KYC and financial crime operations.

  • A background in Financial Crime and Compliance consulting is highly desirable, combined with demonstrable commercial success and a strong sales mindset.

  • Demonstrated ability to construct and close large, strategic, multi-stakeholder services deals, including value proposition, commercial modelling, negotiation and contracting.

  • Practical familiarity with fixed-price, time-and-materials, managed services and outcome-based commercial models, including the ability to assess pricing, margin, risk allocation and delivery implications.

  • Proven experience building account-level services growth plans, identifying whitespace, mapping stakeholders and independently converting insight into qualified opportunities and sustainable pipeline.

  • Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex issues, influence decisions and create urgency with senior client and internal stakeholders.

  • Outstanding relationship management skills and a track record of building trust across client organisations and internal cross-functional teams.

  • Strong commercial acumen, disciplined opportunity management and a consistent record of progressing and closing complex deals while protecting margin, delivery feasibility and deal quality.

  • Experience working across EMEA markets and navigating culturally diverse, matrixed organisations.

Measures of Success

  • Achievement of annual services bookings, revenue and margin targets.

  • Building and maintaining the required level, quality and mix of qualified pipeline coverage against target.

  • Creation of new, independently originated services opportunities from identified account whitespace.

  • Conversion of priority opportunities into large, strategic or multi-year engagements with strong commercial and delivery fundamentals.

  • Development and active progression of actionable services growth plans for priority EMEA accounts.

  • Forecast accuracy, disciplined opportunity progression and timely escalation of commercial or delivery risks.

  • Effective collaboration with regional account teams and successful post-sale handover and continuity through mobilisation and executive checkpoints.

You will have an advantage if you also have:

Personal Profile

  • A confident, credible and highly visible communicator who can make an impact quickly.

  • Client-centric and naturally consultative, with the curiosity to uncover the real business problem and the judgement to shape a compelling response.

  • Commercially sharp, resilient and accountable, with a strong closing orientation and the confidence to lead complex negotiations.

  • Collaborative and low-ego, able to build internal followership and bring diverse specialists together around a winning deal strategy.

  • A self-starting hunter with the strategic discipline to create structure in ambiguity, proactively open doors and independently generate cross-sell and upsell opportunities, taking ownership from whitespace identification to signed engagement.

What’s in it for you?

Learn more about the Benefits at NICE.

Join an ever-growing, market-disrupting, global company where the teams – comprised of the best of the best – work in a fast-paced, collaborative, and creative environment! As the market leader, every day at NICE is a chance to learn and grow, and there are endless internal career opportunities across multiple roles, disciplines, domains, and locations. If you are passionate, innovative, and excited to constantly raise the bar, you may just be our next NICEr!

Additional Information

Travel across EMEA will be required when appropriate to support client engagement, progress strategic opportunities and help close deals.

Requisition ID: 11921
Reporting into: VP, Professional Services

Role Type: Individual Contributor

About NiCE

NICE Ltd. (NASDAQ: NICE) software products are used by 25,000+ global businesses, including 85 of the Fortune 100 corporations, to deliver extraordinary customer experiences, fight financial crime and ensure public safety. Every day, NiCE software manages more than 120 million customer interactions and monitors 3+ billion financial transactions.

Known as an innovation powerhouse that excels in AI, cloud and digital, NiCE is consistently recognized as the market leader in its domains, with over 8,500 employees across 30+ countries.

NiCE is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, neurotype, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation or any other category protected by law.

jobs.title: FP&A Analyst
jobs.excerpt: ConnectWise is an industry and Global leading software company with over 3,000 colleagues in North America, EMEA and APAC.
jobs.description:
ConnectWise is an industry and Global leading software company with over 3,000 colleagues in North America, EMEA and APAC. As a community-driven software company dedicated to the success of technology solution providers, our suite helps over 45,000 of our partners manage their businesses better, sell more efficiently, automate service delivery, and remotely control technology so they can consistently deliver amazing customer experiences.

Our company is powered by our connections, our colleagues, and our community. And, we accept all kinds.

Game-changers, innovators, culture-lovers—and humankind.

We invite discovery and debate. We recognize key moments as milestones.

We see you and value you for your unique contributions. Our inclusive, positive culture lays the foundation to ensure every colleague is valued for their perspectives and skills, giving you the choice of how YOU make a difference.

Curious? Read this opportunity to learn how YOU can make a difference at ConnectWise!

The FP&A Analyst will support strategic decision-making through financial modeling, business-case analysis, and ongoing monitoring of key initiatives. Partnering with the Senior Finance Manager, the analyst will translate financial and operational data into driver-based models, evaluate business scenarios, and prepare clear insights for stakeholders. The role combines project-based analysis with maintenance of established models and tracking of initiative performance. It offers increasing ownership of defined analytical workstreams, with an emphasis on data integrity, transparent assumptions, and documented, repeatable processes.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Build and maintain driver-based financial models supporting strategic initiatives, partnerships, vendor decisions, and growth opportunities.
  • Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to evaluate financial outcomes, key assumptions, and risks.
  • Investigate changes in model outputs and prepare initial conclusions and recommendations for review.
  • Track financial results and operating drivers against business-case assumptions, explaining variances and identifying emerging issues.
  • Refresh established models and reporting as initiatives evolve, coordinating routine inputs with relevant business partners.
  • Support forecasting and multi-year planning projects as needed, including assumption validation and supporting analysis.
  • Source, reconcile, and validate financial and operational data across Adaptive, Power BI, NetSuite, and supporting sources.
  • Investigate reporting discrepancies, validate definitions and mappings, and coordinate resolution with Finance, BI, and other source owners.
  • Maintain model checks, documentation, assumption records, and version controls to strengthen accuracy and shared understanding.
  • Improve repeatable workflows to reduce manual effort and rework while preserving transparent calculations and controls.
  • Independently gather routine inputs and resolve analytical questions with relevant stakeholders.
  • Prepare clear supporting schedules, commentary, and presentation materials for senior finance review.
  • Escalate material assumption, methodology, and data issues with a clear explanation of their implications and proposed next steps.

Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities Required:

  • Relevant experience in FP&A, financial analysis, or another modeling-intensive analytical role.
  • Advanced Excel proficiency, including experience with large, interconnected workbooks, structured references, defined names, external links, and refresh controls.
  • Experience applying AI tools to improve financial modeling, analysis, and reporting workflows, with sound judgment in validating outputs and maintaining accuracy.
  • Strong financial modeling skills, including driver-based forecasts, business cases, and scenario analysis.
  • Demonstrated discipline in source-data reconciliation, model validation, troubleshooting, and documentation.
  • Ability to interrogate Power BI reports and understand how filters, definitions, and reporting scope affect results.
  • Ability to investigate ambiguous issues, organize competing priorities, and distinguish routine corrections from decisions requiring escalation.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to translate detailed analysis into concise business explanations.

Educational/Vocational/Previous Experience Recommendations:

  • Bachelor’s degree in related field or equivalent business experience
  • 2-3 years of relevant experience
  • Preferred: Hands-on experience building and maintaining complex financial models and reconciling financial data across multiple sources
  • Preferred: Experience with SaaS or technology business models

Working Conditions:

  • Onsite/Hybrid/Remote depending on location
  • 0-10% travel may be required

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer - Databases - Analytics | Canada | Remote
jobs.excerpt: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale.
jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote opportunity, and we would be interested in applicants located in the US or Canada.

The Opportunity:

At Grafana Labs, we build observability tools that help users understand, respond to, and improve their systems – regardless of scale, complexity, or tech stack. We recently started a skunkworks initiative with a mission to bring observability to the rest of the business. Our goal is to make Grafana the single best place where humans and AI agents understand and act on real-time data from across the enterprise. As part of this initiative, we are building an AI-native data intelligence system that gives agents reliable, governed access to enterprise context. This system helps agents retrieve the right data, metadata, definitions, lineage, quality signals, and institutional knowledge without every agent builder having to maintain their own brittle context files. The principle is simple: the context system retrieves, agents decide, and data teams maintain the intelligence.

The new team is a mix of seasoned Grafanistas and new hires. We operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership, both as individuals and as a team. Engineers are empowered to make decisions, move quickly, and validate ideas early – while being supported by a deeply collaborative culture that values curiosity, feedback, and cross-functional partnership.

We’re looking for a Senior Software (Database) Engineer to help build the underlying storage system for our general purpose data platform. The database layer has both OLAP and OTLP capabilities to support classic analytics queries while also serving up freshly stored data. It embraces the separation of compute and storage and is designed to run on multiple cloud providers. This is an early-stage role on a high-autonomy team, so you should be comfortable working through ambiguity, making pragmatic architectural decisions, and building systems that can evolve from internal dogfooding to production-grade SaaS. As the team matures, there’s a broad opportunity to expand or redefine this role based on impact and initiative.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Take ownership over and build one or multiple parts of the database: Design, implement, test, and operate ingestion, query planning, distributed query execution, data formats, storage formats.
  • Create a scalable SaaS foundation: Help define and build the architecture for a multi-tenant database service, including tenant isolation, usage tracking, quotas, audit logs, background jobs, and reliable service boundaries.
  • Power agent-facing retrieval workflows: Build APIs and database interfaces that allow AI agents, MCP tools, CLIs, and internal applications to retrieve data quickly.
  • Work across product and infrastructure: Partner with the team to make practical tradeoffs between fast experimentation and long-term reliability, especially as the project moves from prototype to production.
  • Operate what you build: Instrument database services with metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and dashboards. Use observability tools to understand system behavior and improve reliability.
  • Contribute to technical direction: Help shape the architecture, service boundaries, storage choices, API contracts, deployment patterns, and engineering practices for a new product area.
  • Effective communication: You’ll be working in a highly dynamic and collaborative environment, so we need someone who can communicate effectively and contribute across teams.
  • Ownership and impact: Take full ownership of the database solutions you develop, ensuring they are not only innovative but also scalable, maintainable, and aligned with real user workflows.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • Strong engineering skills: Solid experience building production-grade, user-facing software systems. You’re a self-starter, capable of tackling complex engineering problems and making design decisions with minimal supervision.
  • AI experience with a practical mindset: You’re familiar with AI technologies and frameworks, and you focus on delivering high-quality solutions that work in the real world, not just in theory.
  • Quick iteration and experimentation: You’re comfortable releasing prototypes, collecting feedback, and iterating with a pragmatic mindset.
  • Proven initiative: You take ownership and drive projects forward, pushing boundaries to find the most impactful solutions. You can deal with ambiguity and are able to define scope where things are loosely defined.
  • Collaborative attitude: You communicate effectively with your peers. You’re open to feedback, and you bring a solutions-oriented mindset to the table.
  • Experience with distributed systems, catalogs and table formats, query engines.
  • Mastery of a programming language like golang, C++, or Rust
  • Proven track record of delivering software that made it into production and is actively used by users.
  • Exposure to working in cloud-native environments (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).
  • Experience using observability tools to understand and troubleshoot system behavior.

Bonus Points for:

  • Experience building distributed query engines.
  • Experience building data warehouses and/or data lakes.
  • Experience building tools for data engineering.

How we work:

We are a remote-first team that meets regularly over video and does most of our work asynchronously, in writing. We value creativity, diverse perspectives, and clear communication. Tempo is relied upon by prominent global organizations to monitor critical applications and infrastructure, and we expect everyone on the team, including our Staff engineers, to contribute ideas that make it a more reliable, more useful, and more loved product.

Compensation & Rewards:

In Canada, the Base compensation range for this role is $164,490 - $197,389. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:

  • 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
  • Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
  • Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
  • Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
  • Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
  • Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
  • Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
  • Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
  • Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
  • In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
  • Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.

Equal Opportunity Employer:Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.

Grafana Labs may utilize AI tools in its recruitment process to assist in matching information provided in CVs to job postings. The recruitment team will continue to review inbound CVs manually to identify alignment with current openings.

For information about how your personal data is used once you’ve applied to a job, check out our privacy policy.

Who We Are

Pindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions. Powered by the Pindrop Intelligence Network, our unified trust platform helps enterprises answer three critical questions:

Is this identity synthetic? Detect AI-generated and manipulated voice and video.
Is this identity risky? Identify fraud, suspicious behavior, and other risk signals.
Is this identity known? Authenticate identities using voice, device, behavioral, and other signals.

Pindrop brings this intelligence together across purpose-built trust engines to help organizations make informed decisions in real time — protecting customers, workforce interactions, and emerging AI-driven interactions.

Pindrop protects billions of high-risk interactions for enterprises, including leading financial institutions, insurers, and healthcare organizations. Its technology is informed by more than 8 billion real-world interactions annually and protected by 300+ patents.

Recognized by TIME as one of the 10 Most Influential Software Companies of 2026 and by Inc. for Best in Business for Innovation, Pindrop is backed by leading investors including Andreessen Horowitz, IVP, and CapitalG.

  • Participate in on-call rotations, including after-hours support as needed.

  • A technically curious problem-solver with strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.

  • Calm under pressure and confident in handling critical production incidents.

  • Customer-focused, collaborative, and comfortable communicating with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Proactive, accountable, and committed to improving system reliability.

What's in It for You

As a Pindropper, you'll join a growing, remote-first company using innovative voice technology to make security more human. You'll work with talented teams, solve meaningful technical challenges, and help shape the reliability and support experience of Pindrop's platform.

Your First 90 Days

Within 30 Days

  • Complete onboarding and develop an understanding of Pindrop's platform, APIs, and support processes.

  • Begin contributing to technical investigations alongside experienced engineers.

Within 60 Days

  • Independently manage customer cases, API integration issues, and production incidents.

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive technical resolutions.

Within 90 Days

  • Become a trusted technical resource for complex escalations.

  • Contribute improvements to troubleshooting practices, documentation, and support processes.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation, including equity for all employees.

  • Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO).

  • Company-wide rest days.

  • Generous health and welfare plans, including an employer-paid employee-only option.

  • Employer HSA contributions.

  • Vision and dental coverage for you and your family.

  • Employer-provided life and disability insurance.

  • Paid parental leave (equal for all parents).

Senior Manager, Revenue Operations

Role Summary

ChargePoint is looking for a Lead Revenue Accountant & Operations Analyst to champion our end-to-end revenue lifecycle. In this critical role, you will bridge the gap between accounting execution and strategic revenue operations, ensuring the financial integrity of our SaaS, hardware, and services streams. Join us to drive process automation, strengthen our financial frameworks, and support ChargePoint's mission to build the future of e-mobility.

What You Will Be Doing
As the Lead Revenue Operations Analyst and Accountant, you will combine hands-on accounting execution with strategic revenue operations leadership. You will own the revenue lifecycle—from contract review and ASC 606 compliance through journal entries, reconciliations, and close execution. Acting as a strategic bridge between Revenue Accounting, Sales, Legal, and FP&A, you will focus on driving process automation, maintaining audit-ready financial records, and ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of revenue reporting. Success in your first 6–12 months includes streamlining close activities and elevating team performance through proactive problem resolution.

What You Will Bring to ChargePoint

  • Lead the review and analysis of complex sales contracts, purchase orders, and multi-element arrangements to ensure precise revenue recognition under ASC 606.

  • Manage revenue arrangements in NetSuite, configuring and validating start/end dates, revenue schedules, billing data, and subsidiary ledger entries.

  • Drive end-to-end monthly and quarterly revenue close activities, preparing journal entries, revenue deferrals, accruals, and variance analyses.

  • Oversee tracking and milestone-based recognition for project-based revenue, ensuring deliverables are timely and well-documented.

  • Maintain standalone selling price (SSP) allocation models and prepare comprehensive, audit-ready documentation for external auditors and internal SOX compliance.

  • Reconcile revenue data seamlessly across Salesforce, NetSuite, and internal reporting tools to ensure unwavering consistency.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Legal, and Operations, serving as the primary escalation point for revenue coding issues and proactive process fixes.

  • Collaborate with FP&A to support revenue forecasting, partner rebate programs, sales reserves accruals, and ad-hoc financial analysis.

  • Support state and government-funded project revenue, carefully navigating special handling requirements and mixed-product accounting treatments.

  • Champion automation and process improvement initiatives to streamline revenue reporting, reduce manual effort, and strengthen compliance frameworks.

  • Mentor and guide junior revenue analysts and accountants, reviewing their work to elevate team performance and ensure quality compliance.

Requirements

  • 12 - 15 years of progressive experience in revenue accounting, revenue operations, or general accounting, ideally in a SaaS, hardware, or mixed-technology environment.

  • Expert-level understanding of ASC 606, including revenue recognition for multiple performance obligations, variable consideration, and contract modifications.

  • Hands-on expertise with ERP systems (NetSuite strongly preferred) and CRM platforms (Salesforce).

  • Advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets and a methodical approach to close execution and audit documentation.

  • Demonstrated track record of executing process automation, operational improvement projects, and successful external audit/SOX compliance cycles.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field (e.g., B.Com/BBA), CA/CPA qualification, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience utilizing Business Intelligence (BI) tools such as Tableau or Power BI for financial reporting and analytics.

jobs.description:
Dataiku is the Platform for AI Success, the enterprise orchestration layer for building, deploying, and governing AI. In a single environment, teams design and operate analytics, machine learning, and AI agents with the transparency, collaboration, and control enterprises require. Sitting above data platforms, cloud infrastructure, and AI services, Dataiku connects the full enterprise AI stack - empowering organizations to run AI across multi-vendor environments with centralized governance.

The world’s leading companies rely on Dataiku to operationalize AI and run it as a true business performance engine delivering measurable value. For more, visit the Dataiku blog, LinkedIn, X, and YouTube.

About the role

Dataiku is the platform for AI Success, helping organizations put AI to work across their business. The Growth team drives pipeline generation globally through paid media, content syndication, ABM, and marketing operations, and we're looking for a Senior Manager, Lifecycle Marketing to build and own the lifecycle function end to end.

You'll work closely with the VP of Digital & Growth and cross-functional partners across Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success, supporting a global organization across regions. We don't have a lifecycle function today. Email and nurture are secondary responsibilities inside other teams' jobs, so nobody owns what a prospect or customer hears from us, in what order, or how often. There are existing nurture workflows without a current owner and no single view of what runs where, so establishing that visibility is the first priority. You'll build the function from there: the strategy, the systems, the programs, and the team.

What you'll own

The lifecycle operating system

  • One authoritative email and lifecycle calendar across prospect, new-user and customer programs: what goes out, to whom, from which team, and when.
  • Frequency governance, suppression logic and deliverability standards, including being able to say how much of an audience a given send reaches.
  • Segmentation and audience standards, set with the web and marketing ops teams who manage list creation today.
  • A standard for what a lifecycle program needs before it launches: entry criteria, success metric, exit.

Prospect and new-user nurture

  • New-user onboarding and activation nurture: the sequences that move a first touch to an engaged, sales-ready account.
  • Account progression communication: the programs that move accounts from first engagement toward qualified opportunity.
  • Nurture designed around named-account cohorts, built alongside the integrated campaign work so the two don't duplicate each other.
  • Visibility for BDRs into what a lead has already received before they reach out.

Customer lifecycle, retention and expansion

You'll partner closely with Customer Success and Product on this.

  • Programmatic customer nurture: adoption, education, and the sequences that keep users active after initial deployment.
  • Retention and expansion programs, built on account signals rather than calendar cadence.

Automation, data and measurement

  • The lifecycle layer of the marketing automation stack end to end: HubSpot workflows, Salesforce integration, and account and intent data from 6sense.
  • Consolidating the existing nurture workflows into something documented and maintained.
  • Reporting lifecycle contribution in terms the business already uses: engagement progression, influenced pipeline, retention and expansion. You'll build your own reporting rather than wait for a dashboard.
  • The data quality this function depends on, with marketing ops: deliverability, consent, record hygiene.

AI and agentic workflows

  • Lifecycle work inside agentic workflows, rather than AI as a separate experiment. Lifecycle is one of the clearest applications: audience assembly, copy variation, program QA, performance summaries.
  • A standard for what a well-built lifecycle agent looks like, and where human in the loop is required.

Building the function

  • This is the lead role for a function that doesn't exist yet. You'll build the team as the function develops.
  • Getting the rest of the organization aligned on what you're building. Lifecycle touches Web, Content, Acquisition, Field, Marketing Ops, Sales and Customer Success.

What you bring

  • 6+ years in lifecycle, nurture, email or growth marketing in B2B, ideally enterprise software with long, multi-threaded buying cycles.
  • Hands-on marketing automation depth. You've built and owned complex nurture programs yourself. HubSpot or Marketo depth, Salesforce fluency, and real comfort with the data model under both.
  • Command of deliverability, frequency capping, suppression, consent and list hygiene. This role exists partly because nobody has owned these.
  • Experience on both sides of the lifecycle, prospect and customer. If your background covers one, tell us how you'd approach the other.
  • Fluency with intent and account data (6sense, Demandbase or similar), and a view on where it should drive program entry rather than only reporting.
  • Comfort building with AI, expected rather than optional. No engineering background needed. You should already be using LLMs in your own work, with a view on where they belong in lifecycle programs and where human in the loop is required.
  • Analytical strength. You can define a metric, instrument it, and defend it, including when the honest answer is that the current number isn't reliable.
  • Comfort with a build role: ambiguity, direct conversations about tradeoffs, and establishing a function through influence before you have a team.
  • Experience working across regions in a global organization.
  • Excellent written English. Other languages welcome, not required.

Why this role

Lifecycle is unowned at Dataiku today. This role defines it, reporting to the VP who owns the function, with a mandate to build the team behind it.

What are you waiting for!

At Dataiku, you'll be part of a journey to shape the ever-evolving world of AI. We're not just building a product; we're crafting the future of AI. If you're ready to make a significant impact in a company that values innovation, collaboration, and your personal growth, we can't wait to welcome you to Dataiku! Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Security Incident Response team works to analyze, investigate, and respond to threats before they impact Stripe’s business or users. From external attacks to insider threats, our goal is to respond with speed and precision, remediate, and support the incident postmortem process. The team is distributed, working across multiple AMER time zones, and will regularly coordinate with stakeholders in EMEA and APAC.

What you’ll do

You will leverage your security engineering experience to improve incident response capabilities at Stripe. With an emphasis on user and entity behavior analytics, as well as endpoint hardening, you will gain a deep understanding of Stripe’s systems, tooling, and workflows to be able to differentiate between legitimate and malicious activity. Using both threat intelligence and collected telemetry, you will guide and build Stripe-specific signals enrichment logic and incident response solutions that scale with our company. Lastly, your analytic capabilities will be critical during security incidents to reduce uncertainty, uncover root causes, and inform future prevention and detection mechanisms.

Responsibilities

  • Analyze and investigate a broad range of threats or activities occurring on client devices
  • Develop requirements for detection models and enhancements to existing systems
  • Collect, transform, and ingest raw data from disparate sources into threat detection pipelines
  • Streamline incident response capabilities, ensuring the tooling and processes are clear
  • Work cross-functionally with security engineering and data science teams to build solutions for analyzing security events data at scale and protecting Stripe networks, systems, and data from threats
  • Provide actionable insights to help identify, prevent, detect, and respond to anomalous or potentially malicious user and entity activity
  • Act as the subject-matter expert and primary contact for stakeholder teams invested in Security Analytics and Detection programs as well as Stripe-wide security initiatives
  • Collaborate effectively with teammates, leading projects, mentoring others, and developing and championing quality standards within the team

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

  • 3+ years experience analyzing large data sets to solve problems and/or building models with a behavioral approach to security

  • Ability to communicate results clearly and focus on impact
  • Ability to think creatively and holistically about reducing risk in a complex environment

  • Familiarity with common open-source frameworks for big data processing and/or data science (PySpark, Pandas, Sci-kit Learn, etc.)

jobs.title: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - US
jobs.excerpt: Allocator One Group is a global investing platform redefining how institutional capital reaches private markets.
jobs.description:
Allocator One Group is a global investing platform redefining how institutional capital reaches private markets. We operate through two synergistic businesses:

  • Allocator One backs exceptional first- and second-time fund managers around the world—acting as “seed-investor + platform” for emerging VC funds.
  • Infra One, our fund-ops and tech arm, provides the regulatory, administrative, and tech infrastructure that allows those new funds to scale rapidly and globally. We are already live and serving in the UK, US, Austria, Germany and launching Singapore, India and Luxembourg imminently.

Together, we deliver both the capital and the structure fund managers need—and in doing so build a global ecosystem of platforms, people, and ideas that reshape private markets.

This role is one of the four foundational roles that we are hiring for to establish Infra One's US operating platform. These are not narrow, siloed functions. Each role is an architect of the Infra One US operating system—building the regulatory, operational, and financial infrastructure that will enable dozens of GPs to scale with confidence.

Tasks

The Role: Architect of Regulatory Credibility

The CCO sits at the intersection of the SEC, Infra One's platform vision, and every GP who will depend on our compliance infrastructure. You are not a compliance checker; you are the designer of the entire regulatory operating system for a European platform entering the most complex financial markets in the world.

You will own SEC registration (Form ADV), policy architecture, compliance monitoring across multiple fund vehicles, and the relationship with securities regulators. More broadly, you are Infra One's second-most senior regulatory voice after the US Platform Head, directly shaping strategic decisions about fund structuring, delegation models, and GP onboarding.

Key Responsibilities

Regulatory Foundation

  • Lead the SEC registration process as a private fund adviser (Form ADV Part 1A, 1B, and Part 2 Adviser Brochure) and manage ongoing compliance.
  • Design and implement written compliance policies covering portfolio management, conflicts of interest, fiduciary duties, custody oversight, and AML/KYC frameworks.
  • Conduct annual compliance reviews and testing; prepare SEC examination responses and handle any regulatory inquiries.
  • Stay current with evolving SEC private fund rules (Reg PF, current enforcement priorities) and translate them into practical Infra One policies.

Operational Substance

  • Define staffing, systems, and office infrastructure requirements to meet SEC expectations for "adequate" organizational substance (not formulaic, but credible).
  • Establish procedures for monitoring sub-advised GPs and ensuring they comply with fund mandates and risk limits.
  • Oversee books and records management (6-year retention, email preservation, trade capture, decision logs) and coordinate with IT on cybersecurity compliance.

Multi-Fund Governance

  • Design and oversee compliance monitoring across Infra One's portfolio of funds (each with its own structure and GP).
  • Conduct initial and ongoing due diligence on each GP sub-adviser: qualifications, compliance history, operational capabilities, conflicts of interest.
  • Maintain evidence of monitoring (quarterly reviews, compliance testing, incident logs) to demonstrate SEC-level governance.

Advisor to Platform

  • Advise the US Platform Head on fund structuring choices (Delaware LP vs. LLC, feeder structures, co-investment), GP selection, and investor eligibility questions.
  • Participate in investment committee meetings to flag compliance or regulatory risks early.
  • Own conflicts of interest identification and disclosure; ensure all material conflicts are documented and communicated to fund investors.

Requirements

What You Bring

Experience & Expertise

  • 7–12 years of compliance experience at a registered investment adviser (RIA), private fund platform, hedge fund, or PE firm.
  • Deep knowledge of the Advisers Act, Reg D, Form ADV, and SEC examination standards for private fund advisers.
  • Hands-on experience with multi-fund governance, sub-adviser monitoring, and conflicts of interest management.
  • Familiarity with custody rules, AML/KYC frameworks, and cybersecurity compliance standards.
  • Prior experience with SEC registration, Form ADV filings, and exam cycles.

Mindset & Approach

  • Entrepreneurial compliance mindset: you thrive in ambiguity and build frameworks from scratch rather than inheriting them.
  • Cross-functional fluency: you speak the language of operations, finance, and legal—not just compliance.
  • Practical and proportionate: you understand when regulation requires substance and when it allows flexibility.
  • Communicator: you can distill complex regulatory requirements into actionable policy for non-compliance teams.

Nice to Have

  • Prior exposure to European fund regulation (Luxembourg, Ireland) or multi-jurisdictional platforms.
  • CPA, JD, or CFA; CCEP (Certified Compliance and Ethics Professional) is a plus.
  • Exposure to infrastructure or venture fund management.

Benefits

  • Location: Remote (preferred US timezone overlap with San Francisco HQ)
  • Salary Range: $200,000–$280,000 base + 20% bonus
  • Equity: TBD (0.1%–0.3% depending on background)
  • Reports to: US Platform Head / Managing Director
  • Hiring Timeline: Month 0–1

Why This Role Matters

The CCO is Infra One's regulatory anchor. Without credible, well-documented compliance infrastructure, no GP will trust the platform, and no institutional LP will commit capital. You are building the proof of competence that enables scale.

Why Infra One

  • Leverage: Build a compliance framework once, then deploy it across dozens of GPs. Your work scales exponentially.
  • Autonomy: Full ownership of the compliance operating system; direct input into platform strategy and GP selection.
  • Visibility: Reporting directly to the MD; participation in investment decisions and board discussions.
  • Global impact: Help reshape how emerging infrastructure and venture managers access US capital.
  • Equity upside: Early-stage role with meaningful equity stake in a platform targeting the largest capital markets in the world.

jobs.description:
Responsibilities

As a key Associate in the Nuclear Power Group (NPG), you will have the opportunity to aid, participate and coordinate engineers and other professionals involved in support of License Renewal (LR) / Subsequent License Renewal (SLR) license extension, and post-approval implementation activities across the U.S. nuclear power fleet.

S&L is seeking an experienced License Renewal (LR) / Subsequent License Renewal (SLR) professional to support license extension and post-approval implementation activities across the U.S. nuclear power fleet. This role focuses on turning LR/SLR commitments and aging management program (AMP) requirements into practical, field-executable inspection and implementation plans. It can also include performing visual inspections (e.g., VT-1/VT-2 or similar).

The ideal candidate brings experience with LR/SLR application and implementation and an optional combination of nuclear engineering programs, field trade experience (e.g., operations or maintenance), work management/scheduling, NRC submittals and/or inspections, and can bridge between technical aging management requirements, work management systems, and field execution.

Key Responsibilities

License renewal & aging management implementation

  • Support LR/SLR implementation activities such as procedure changes, preventive maintenance (PM) basis and frequency development, work order (WO) development and review, and nuclear program basis document updates.
  • Roadmap required inspections and aging management activities to comply with NRC regulations, LR/SLR commitments, and applicable AMPs.
  • Define and help maintain sample populations and inspection scopes (e.g., one-time inspections, selective leaching, tank inspections) and ensure results are traceable to LR/SLR commitments and program requirements.

Work Management & Coordination Responsibilities

  • Use work management and planning systems (e.g., WOs, PMs, work items) to identify and capture LR/SLR opportunities in both online and outage scopes.
  • Screen and analyze large WO and PM lists (often thousands of line items) to identify high-value inspection opportunities based on system, component, material, and environment.
  • Coordinate with schedulers, planners, and field organizations to embed aging management needs into realistic work sequences and outage plans.

Engineering basis, documentation & configuration control

  • Develop and maintain engineering program basis documentation, including AMP basis, PM basis, and supporting technical justifications.
  • Perform data validation, engineering change tracking, and configuration control for LR/SLR-related documents and commitments.
  • Support NRC commitment tracking and closure, including preparing or reviewing technical responses, inspection packages, and closure documentation.

Stakeholder engagement & SME coordination

  • Interact with clients and NRC in a technical expert role, clearly explaining aging management strategies, inspection plans, and results.
  • Work closely with mechanical, electrical, and structural SMEs, program owners, and field leads to refine scopes, aging mechanisms, and documentation expectations.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement, technology-forward thinking, and cross-functional collaboration across engineering, planning, and implementation teams.

Regulatory awareness & operating experience

  • Maintain awareness of changes in LR/SLR and aging management regulations, guidance, and industry operating experience.
  • Incorporate relevant NUREGs, NEI guidance, and industry OE into program basis documents, implementation strategies, and inspection plans.

Qualifications

We do not sponsor employees for work authorization in the U.S. for this position.

Essential Skills

  • An associate’s degree or equivalent experience.
  • 5 or more years of experience in the design and analysis of nuclear, industrial, or DOE facilities.
  • Proven experience managing and/or participating in multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Experience in managing medium-to-large critical projects.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience in providing guidance, mentoring, and training to staff engineers
  • Licensed Operator for a Utility
  • Experience delivering accurate, high-quality technical documentation in a highly regulated environment (nuclear, DOE, or equivalent).
  • Familiarity with engineering documentation systems, nuclear QA/QC protocols, and configuration management processes.
  • Strong systems thinking skills, with the ability to balance innovation with compliance, safety, and traceability.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with work management systems (e.g., work orders, PMs, planning tools) and to align technical requirements with implementable work packages and schedules.
  • Proven capability to collaborate with SMEs and field organizations, using drawings, histories, prior WOs, and data to converge on practical implementation solutions.

Preferred Experience

License renewal, SLR, and aging management

  • Prior involvement in license renewal, subsequent license renewal, or nuclear aging management programs, including development or implementation of AMPs, one-time inspections, or selective leaching programs.
  • Experience with NRC, INPO, or DOE regulations, and participation in NRC audits or inspections (e.g., Inspection Procedure 71003 or similar).
  • Familiarity with key nuclear industry LR/SLR documents such as NUREG‑1800, NUREG‑1801, NEI 95‑10, NUREG‑2191, NUREG‑2192, NUREG‑2221, NEI 17‑01, and/or NUREG‑1555.
  • Participation and/or familiarity with the Nuclear Energy Institute (NEI) License Renewal Task Force or similar industry working groups.

Background experience

  • Strong practical understanding of mechanical systems and components (pumps, valves, strainers, tanks, heat exchangers, piping) and how work is actually performed on them in the field.
  • Ability to connect materials and environments to aging mechanisms (e.g., loss of material, pitting, erosion, selective leaching, coating degradation) and to define what inspections need to observe and document.
  • Background in one or more of the following: mechanical maintenance/engineering, system engineering, NDE/inspection, chemistry/corrosion engineering, or field construction/trades (e.g., piping, welding, valve maintenance) that provides credibility with craft and insight into how design, procedures, and work orders translate into physical work.
  • Several years in a nuclear work management / outage or online planning, system engineering, or maintenance engineering role, preferably with exposure to LR/SLR implementation or aging management programs.
  • Prior hands-on or close-support experience with plant modification or maintenance on mechanical systems (e.g., as a maintenance engineer, system engineer, field engineer, NDE/inspection engineer, or craft/trades lead) in a nuclear or similarly regulated environment.
  • Experience working in cross-functional project teams (engineering, programs, planning, field, and external consultants) to deliver complex, multi-outage implementation scopes.

Technology & Innovation

Sargent & Lundy values the appropriate use of technology to improve how work gets done and deliver high-quality outcomes for our clients. Depending on the role, employees may use data, automation, artificial intelligence, and other digital tools to support research, analysis, engineering and design activities, workflow improvement, or other aspects of their work. We value candidates who demonstrate an interest in learning and effectively using emerging technologies where relevant to their role. Employees remain accountable for their work and are expected to apply appropriate professional judgment and review when using technology-assisted tools. Experience with AI, automation, programming, or similar technologies is valued where relevant but is not required unless specifically identified elsewhere in the job description.

About Sargent & Lundy

At Sargent & Lundy, we care about the health and well-being of our employees. Our commitment extends beyond the workplace, offering comprehensive healthcare plans and generous paid time off to support our team members in every aspect of their lives. We understand the importance of work-life balance, which is why we are proud to provide competitive, award-winning benefits. Our dedication to employee satisfaction has earned us the prestigious Top Workplaces Culture Excellence Award for compensation and benefits in 2022, 2023, and 2024.

jobs.excerpt: Description MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.
jobs.description:
Description

MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi’s technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality.

As our Product Manager for Insurance, you’ll own an entirely new product line: bringing insurance payments to a platform that today runs almost entirely on self-pay. You’ll build eligibility, prior authorization, and claims into a business already handling ~18,000 visits a month, a genuine zero-to-one effort that opens a new revenue stream for the company.You’ll own the “coverage truth” (eligibility and benefits, the payer → plan → coverage data model, and cost-share), the economics of the insurance model, prior authorization flows, and the path from visit to claim to payment. You’ll work at the intersection of clinical, finance, engineering, and legal, partnering with a cross-functional pod of engineers and QA that will grow as the line scales.

Why this role:

  • Zero-to-one ownership. You’re standing up an entire insurance product line from scratch inside a profitable, working telehealth business
  • Measured impact. Your work opens a new revenue stream, and success is measured in insured visits paid at the expected rate, denial rate, and time to cash, not features shipped.
  • Breadth and real influence. You’ll operate across clinical, finance, product, and engineering, owning the systems a dozen stakeholders depend on and driving the decisions that unblock launch.

Responsibilities

  • Own insurance as a product line. The insurance team is the centre of product decisions for everything insurance touches.
  • Launch insurance end to end. Map how insurance should work at MEDvidi, prototype it, and validate it against real cases with revenue-cycle staff, coordinators and patients. Take every decision blocking launch to the people who own it, with a recommendation and a deadline, and coordinate the launch across teams and vendors.
  • Coverage. Eligibility and benefits checks, the payer → plan → coverage data model, and cost-share (copay, deductible, coinsurance), so every booking gets a correct answer on coverage and on what the patient owes before the visit.
  • Patient money. Estimates before the visit, collecting copay and deductible, balances after the payer adjudicates, statements, superbills for out-of-network patients, and the rules for when an insured patient can still pay cash.
  • Prior authorisation. From prescription to medication in hand, plus visit authorisations where payers require them.
  • Visit to claim to payment. With the team, build the full revenue-cycle loop: claims, clearinghouse, remittance, denials and appeals.

This role is not for you if:

  • You want a defined roadmap and clean requirements handed to you: here, the requirements don’t exist yet, and you build them from knowledge scattered across teams and vendors.
  • You think of the job as shipping features as specified, rather than owning a business outcome you can measure in money.
  • You wait for authority before you act, or you’re uncomfortable driving and escalating decisions with people who don’t report to you.

Requirements

  • 6+ years senior-level product management experience, including ownership of complex, systems-heavy products where a change in one place ripples into many others under high uncertainty.
  • A track record of turning stakeholder requests and feature “wants” into the real business problem worth solving, cutting what isn’t needed and reframing what is.
  • An ownership mindset: you build alignment across teams through context and arguments, not authority; come with a clear proposal (“here’s how I suggest this works”); and when a decision stalls, bring options and a recommendation to the people who need to weigh in, rather than waiting for someone else to decide.
  • Outcome-driven to the core: you measure yourself in business results: denial rate, time to cash and you dig into the data yourself to find where value leaks.
  • Advanced English (C1+) your primary stakeholders are US-based and fluent Russian.
  • Remote, with working hours that overlap the team in CET and some overlap with US-based stakeholders.

Would be a plus:

  • Hands-on familiarity with US health insurance and the revenue cycle: eligibility and benefits, prior authorization, claims, denials, and reimbursement.
  • AI as a working tool: you use tools like Claude and Cursor to prototype and iterate fast, and you know where AI should and shouldn’t be applied.
  • Experience building something zero-to-one in a regulated environment (HIPAA or similar).

What we offer

  • High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space.
  • Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package.
  • Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model.
  • Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation.
  • Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply.
  • Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days.
  • Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events.

Ready to make an impact? Send us your profile, let’s build something meaningful together.

MEDvidi is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and contractors. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Hey there!

We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

About the role:

This role will be focused on understanding and reducing the security risk of Fever's cloud infrastructure and data. You will run technical risk assessments of our AWS environments, data platforms and new architectures, identify the weaknesses that could lead to a security incident or a data breach, and work with the owning teams until those risks are fixed.

As part of the Cybersecurity team, you will focus on defensive security in cloud and data environments: where our sensitive data lives, who and what can access it, how it is protected, and how secure the infrastructure underneath is. This is an exciting opportunity to make a tangible impact in a high-growth global category leader, working alongside experts to implement best practices and innovative security solutions. If you're passionate about cloud and data security and enjoy tackling challenges in a dynamic environment, we’d love to have you on board!

What would you do at Fever?

In your first month at Fever:

  • You will be fully integrated into the team. You will participate in planning and follow-up meetings with other areas.
  • You will meet the departments of Fever.
  • You will get familiar with Fever's technological structure and ecosystem (applications, infrastructure, data platforms, architecture, etc.)
  • You will gain an understanding of our security processes, tools, risk methodology, and overall security landscape.

After 3 months at Fever:

  • You will run infrastructure and architecture risk assessments using our risk methodology.
  • You will map where sensitive data is stored and processed (S3, databases, data warehouse, SaaS) and who can access it.
  • You will participate in security configuration reviews to ensure cloud and data environments meet industry standards.
  • You will develop automation to detect data exposure, excessive permissions, and misconfigurations.
  • You will participate in vulnerability management sessions, collaborating with stakeholders to drive continuous security improvements.

On your 6th month in Fever:

  • You will own the risk assessment process for infrastructure and data, from design reviews to risk acceptance.
  • You will drive the remediation of the main data and infrastructure risks with clear owners and deadlines.
  • You will lead initiatives to implement secure solutions for data: classification, encryption and key management, and least-privilege access.
  • You will act as a point of contact for technical guidance on cloud architecture, data security, and configurations.
  • You will develop cybersecurity technical documentation and secure best-practice guidelines to educate and support stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Perform technical risk assessments and threat models of cloud infrastructure, data platforms and new architectures, and document residual risk.
  • Maintain the infrastructure and data risk register, prioritising risks and tracking treatment plans with owners.
  • Identify, classify and protect sensitive data across AWS services, data warehouses and SaaS (data security posture).
  • Review and enforce encryption, key management (KMS), network isolation and identity and access controls for data stores.
  • Conduct regular security assessments to identify vulnerabilities and misconfigurations in the AWS ecosystem.
  • Develop and deploy automated security solutions to detect, report, and remediate data exposure and misconfigurations.
  • Collaborate with Data, DevOps, and engineering teams to build security into data pipelines and infrastructure.

About you

Must have:

  • Proven experience performing security risk assessments of cloud infrastructure and architectures (threat modeling, likelihood/impact, residual risk).
  • Strong experience with AWS cloud infrastructure security including IAM, networking, KMS, S3, logging and organisation-level controls.
  • Good understanding of data security: data classification, encryption, access governance and data loss prevention.
  • Experience securing data platforms (e.g., data lakes, Redshift, Snowflake, Databricks, or similar) and their pipelines.
  • Proficiency in scripting for automation and security operations (Python, Go, or similar).
  • Knowledge of risk and cloud security frameworks (ISO 27005, NIST SP 800-53, CIS Benchmarks, CSA CCM).
  • Ability to work cross-functionally and explain risk to technical and business audiences.

It would be a plus if you have:

  • Experience with the use of AI and agentic processes to enhance efficiency and provide stronger technical capabilities.
  • Experience with Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), CNAPP or CSPM tools.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation, or similar).
  • Knowledge of privacy regulations affecting data (GDPR) and PCI DSS.
  • Security certifications (e.g., CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, CRISC, CISSP or similar).

Commission: 12% on new sales cash collected; 10% ongoing residual commissions
Primary Market: Independent U.S. car dealerships, particularly buy-here-pay-here dealerships
Start: As soon as mutually agreed

About the Company

Our client is an established digital marketing agency that helps independent U.S. car dealerships generate qualified leads and grow vehicle sales through Meta Ads, CRM solutions, and lead-generation services.

The Opportunity

The agency is looking for a consultative, results-driven Full-Cycle Sales Closer to take ownership of the sales pipeline and take over day-to-day sales responsibilities from the founder.

You'll manage every opportunity from initial contact and qualification through discovery, presentation, objection handling, follow-up, and close. You'll report directly to the founder, help build a repeatable sales process, and have the opportunity to grow into a sales leadership role as the company grows.

The core offer is a $2,500 month-to-month marketing service or a $6,000 three-month package paid upfront.

Inbound and Warm First

This is primarily an inbound and warm-lead role. Opportunities come mainly from Meta Ads, warm referrals, existing relationships, and industry events. Independent cold prospecting is not the primary requirement.

  • Projected volume: 40–60 booked sales calls per month
  • Target close rate: 30–40% of sales calls, with 50% representing exceptional performance
  • Actual lead flow may vary

What You'll Do

Full-Cycle Sales & Closing

  • Promptly contact and qualify inbound leads and warm prospects from referrals, existing contacts, and industry events
  • Schedule and confirm appointments, run consultative sales calls, present the offer, handle objections, and close deals, collecting payment during the call whenever possible
  • Build trust with independent dealership owners and decision-makers through professional, consultative conversations
  • Maintain persistent, professional follow-up with qualified opportunities to reduce no-shows and lost deals
  • Hand closed clients over to onboarding, keep up periodic commercial follow-up, and identify relevant upsell opportunities

Pipeline Ownership & Sales Operations

  • Own the pipeline end to end, keeping CRM records, deal stages, follow-up tasks, and forecasts accurate
  • Track lead response, booked appointments, show rates, close rates, cash collected, and recurring revenue
  • Work closely with the founder to refine messaging, qualification criteria, sales presentations, and follow-up processes
  • Share frontline feedback on prospect objections, lead quality, offer positioning, and campaign effectiveness

Founder Collaboration & Growth

  • Report directly to the founder and own day-to-day sales execution
  • Help establish a repeatable sales process and support future sales hires as the pipeline grows
  • Take part in ongoing professional development and potentially train future sales team members
  • Attend occasional U.S. industry conferences and trade shows (approximately 2–3 per year)

Earning Potential

Base Pay (Temporary)
$3,000–$4,000 USD/month plus commissions for the initial 1–2 months, depending on ramp-up progress. The temporary base supports your ramp-up and is removed once you're fully ramped.

Commission on New Sales

12% of initial cash collected:

  • Monthly offer: $300 on a $2,500 initial payment
  • Prepaid offer: $720 on a $6,000 three-month upfront payment

Ongoing Residuals
10% of subsequent recurring payments from clients you personally close, for as long as they remain active and paying. Residuals have no stated time limit.

After Ramp-Up
Compensation is commission and recurring residuals only. Earnings are performance-dependent and are not guaranteed. Final payment mechanics and ramp-up terms are set out in the written agreement.

Career Path

As the company grows, a high-performing closer may have the opportunity to train new sales hires and progress into a Lead Salesperson or Sales Manager position. Leadership responsibilities and related compensation would be agreed separately. Advancement is optional and not guaranteed.

How to Apply

Submit an updated resume highlighting your personally closed deals, average deal sizes, sales-cycle length, and relevant recurring-revenue experience. Examples of selling to business owners, especially dealerships or other local businesses, and of selling digital marketing services are a plus.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • Ideally 3–5 years of proven full-cycle B2B sales experience; exceptional candidates with a shorter track record may be considered
  • Proven success selling recurring services or comparable high-ticket business solutions, with the ability to explain your individual sales metrics and outcomes
  • Excellent spoken English, a professional video-call presence, and the ability to build rapport with U.S. dealership owners
  • Strong understanding of digital marketing agency services, particularly Meta Ads and lead generation
  • Strong CRM discipline, consistent follow-up, initiative, resilience, and comfort with performance-based compensation
  • Based in the United States
  • Core availability from 9:00 AM–5:00 PM Central Time, with flexibility for prospect appointments
  • Professional communication, punctuality, and a focus on measurable sales outcomes

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling to independent car dealerships or working in the automotive industry
  • Direct experience closing digital marketing or lead-generation agency retainers
  • Success in shorter-cycle consultative B2B sales environments
  • Experience building warm referral networks and converting event-generated opportunities
  • Familiarity with GoHighLevel or a comparable CRM (direct GoHighLevel experience is not required)
  • Previous team leadership experience, or clear potential to develop into a Sales Manager / Head of Sales role

Benefits

  • Temporary base pay of $3,000–$4,000 USD/month during your initial 1–2 month ramp-up, plus commissions
  • 12% commission on new sales cash collected
  • 10% recurring residual commissions on clients you personally close, with no stated time limit while they remain active and paying
  • 100% remote work within the United States
  • Flexible schedule around core hours of 9:00 AM–5:00 PM CT
  • Primarily inbound and warm opportunities from Meta Ads, referrals, existing relationships, and industry events
  • Weekly growth and professional development training
  • Company-covered travel to U.S. industry conferences and trade shows (approximately 2–3 per year)
  • Direct collaboration with the founder and ownership of the full sales cycle
  • Potential path to Lead Salesperson or Sales Manager as the company grows
