jobs.excerpt: About Gaggle Your work can help save students’ lives.
jobs.description:
About Gaggle

Your work can help save students’ lives. For over 25 years, Gaggle has partnered with K-12 schools on student safety, and our team has helped save more than 8,600 student lives since 2018. Our technology flags signs of concern in students’ digital activity, our trained safety professionals review them around the clock so the right people can step in before a crisis, and our coaching and therapy services help students get support afterward. Today we serve more than 6 million students in over 1,500 districts, and protecting their data is central to that trust.

Join our fully remote team, named a 2026 Top Workplace for remote work.

The opportunity
Salesforce & Salesforce Health Cloud are the system our sales, customer success and therapy teams rely on every day. In this role, you’ll own it for them, end to end, and you’ll be as comfortable in a discovery conversation with a sales leader as in a complex Flow. This is a remote, full-time role on our Technology team.

You’ll work directly with business stakeholders to understand what they’re trying to achieve, often before it’s a clear requirement, then design the Salesforce solution, build it, release it and stand behind it in production. There’s no layer of management translating requirements or reviewing every decision. You’ll make the call and own how it turns out, with your manager aligned with you on priorities, not the details. You’ll also work closely with another experienced Salesforce administrator and help them grow through coaching.

What you'll do

  • Turn business needs into Salesforce solutions. Sit down with sales, customer success and therapy leaders, figure out what they actually need, and recommend a design, including what you’d deliberately leave out.
  • Build it, ship it, own it. Design the data model and Flows, test and release the change, and stay with it until it runs cleanly in production. When something breaks, you find the root cause.
  • Pay down Salesforce tech debt. Untangle inherited automation and configuration, retire what no longer earns its place, and favor clicks over code so the next person can maintain what you built.
  • Keep Salesforce running day to day. Users and permissions, reports and dashboards, and support and training for the teams who depend on it.
  • Protect sensitive data. Student and clinical data lives in our org, so you’ll own the security, sharing and data quality that keep it safe and trustworthy.
  • Work AI-first. Use AI tools, including Claude and Salesforce’s own AI, to move faster on Flows, configuration, data cleanup and documentation, and check the output before it reaches production.
  • Raise the bar. Review designs, coach a fellow Salesforce administrator, and help stakeholders make good prioritization calls.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of hands-on Salesforce experience, including complex solutions you owned in production yourself, not only supported.
  • Deep platform knowledge. You know Flow, configuration, security and sharing, and data modeling well, and you know where the platform’s limits are.
  • Design judgment. You lay out the options, explain the trade-offs and pick the simplest solution that will hold up. You know when a problem can be solved with configuration and when it really needs custom code.
  • Business fluency. You’re comfortable working with the business, with sales, customer success and business leaders, you ask the questions that get to the real need, and you explain technical trade-offs in plain terms.
  • Ownership without oversight. You’ve made consequential calls on your own and stood behind the results.
  • Production discipline. You’ve led complex releases with real testing and rollback plans, and traced production issues back to the root cause.
  • Care with sensitive data. Experience with regulated data (HIPAA, FERPA or similar) or with Health Cloud is a plus.
  • AI-forward. You use AI tools every day and know when their output needs a second look.
  • A coach’s instinct. You’ve mentored or reviewed the work of other admins, and you enjoy helping someone grow.
  • Always learning. You pick up new parts of the platform on your own and take feedback well.

Our Team Commitment
Gaggle is proud to be recognized as a 2026 Remote Top Workplace. We are committed to equal opportunity without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.description:
Program Manager

WorkLife Law

Classification: Class Code 1740 / Level 3 / Exempt / Full-Time / Represented / Benefited

Work Arrangement: Fully Remote

Anticipated hiring range: $75,000 - $85,000 (commensurate with experience)

Term: One-year term, with the initial appointment and subsequent renewal contingent upon the continuation of grant funding. (WorkLife Law has been awarded a grant that runs through December 2029 that will cover all costs associated with this position.)

ABOUT WORKLIFE LAW

WorkLife Law is a national advocacy and research organization that advances gender and racial equity by strengthening legal rights for pregnant people and family caregivers. Our work seeks to ensure all people have the freedom to build and maintain economic security through employment and educational opportunities, without having to sacrifice their health or their loved ones’ care. As a center of the University of California College of the Law, San Francisco, WorkLife Law provides direct assistance to workers and students in need and addresses structural inequality by changing public policy at the state and national levels.

Current areas of focus include fighting for reproductive justice; preventing discrimination against family caregivers; promoting legal rights for pregnant and lactating workers; operating the nation’s only legal resource center for pregnant and parenting students; and ensuring equitable access to leave. Learn more on Our Impact page.

THE ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Program Manager will primarily support WorkLife Law’s new initiative: Expecting Change: Supporting Pregnant and Postpartum Workers. This program will train healthcare providers on their patients’ workplace rights during pregnancy and postpartum and provide free legal assistance to pregnant and postpartum workers through WorkLife Law’s free legal helpline.

Working closely with the WorkLife Law attorneys who deliver trainings to healthcare providers and serve helpline callers, the Program Manager will identify training opportunities, coordinate training outreach and logistics, track and analyze program data, manage the project’s consultant and vendor relationships, and draft narrative and financial reports to program funders. This position will also support organization-wide operations that align with Expecting Change program responsibilities. The Program Manager will report directly to WorkLife Law’s Senior Operations & Finance Manager.

This role is best suited for an individual who is highly organized, who enjoys building systems that help a small team work efficiently, and who takes pride in getting the details right.

Typical duties and responsibilities consist of, but are not limited to:

Expecting Change Operations and Logistics

  • Coordinate with WorkLife Law attorneys to develop a pipeline of healthcare provider training opportunities, including researching medical schools, hospitals, community health centers, professional associations, and conferences of interest and conducting tailored outreach to secure training engagements
  • Schedule trainings and coordinate logistics with host institutions and WorkLife Law attorneys, including calendaring, technology, materials, and continuing education credit requirements
  • Coordinate production and distribution of educational materials, such as exam room posters for distribution through healthcare provider partners
  • Coordinate meetings for the healthcare provider advisory committee, including scheduling, distributing agendas, taking notes, coordinating post-meeting follow-up tasks, and processing stipend payments
  • Consistently track project timelines and deliverables and coordinate with project staff to ensure the project remains on track to meet established metrics
  • Support logistics for related hiring processes and assist with onboarding and offboarding of program staff
  • Support the management of related IT assets and software accounts, including user access

Data, Evaluation, and Systems

  • Administer pre- and post-training surveys, track results, and prepare summaries that inform improvements to training content
  • Maintain accurate records of trainings delivered, audiences reached, related helpline activity, and other program metrics
  • Manage and improve databases and workflows, including helpline intake and tracking in Kintone and automations in Zapier
  • Optimize WorkLife Law’s use of data systems, including Mailchimp contact lists
  • Draft and maintain Standard Operating Procedure documents for any program-specific and related operations processes

Grant Reporting and Management

  • Serve as the primary drafter and project manager for narrative and financial reports to Expecting Change program funders: gathering information from attorneys and Co-Directors and ensuring reports are accurate, complete, and submitted on time
  • Track grant deliverables, deadlines, and reporting requirements across program funders
  • Monitor program budgets and grant spending in partnership with the Senior Operations and Finance Manager, flagging variances and helping ensure funds are spent according to grant agreements
  • Support the ongoing optimization of WorkLife Law’s grant reporting and management

Finance and Contracts

In partnership with the Senior Operations and Finance Manager, this position will help:

  • Process invoices, payments, and expense documentation, ensuring costs are allocated correctly across funding sources
  • Draft and track consultant and vendor contracts in coordination with the law school’s purchasing department, and monitor deliverables and payments
  • Identify vendors when needed and solicit bids
  • Support budget tracking, forecasting, and year-end reconciliation

In addition to the responsibilities outlined above, the Program Manager should proactively identify and propose ideas that improve efficiency and effectiveness across WorkLife Law. The position may also perform other related functions as needs arise.

REQUIREMENTS

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education and Experience

  • At least three years of project management, program operations, or nonprofit operations experience; professional experience with non-profit social justice organizations and/or health institutions strongly preferred
  • Experience with grant reporting and budget tracking preferred

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Commitment to gender, racial, and class equity, disability and reproductive justice
  • Strong project management skills, including the ability to track many moving parts, set timelines, and follow up to ensure deadlines are met
  • Acute attention to detail
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize time to meet deadlines for multiple projects, including the nimbleness to shift between long-term and time-sensitive tasks
  • Strong writing and editing skills, including the ability to draft clear, accurate reports that describe program activities and results for funders
  • Comfort working with budgets, spreadsheets, and data, and presenting that information clearly
  • Ability to effectively use Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel), Google Workspace, project management tools like Asana, database tools like Kintone, video conferencing tools like Zoom, blast email programs like Mailchimp; and ability to pick up other software and applications quickly
  • Ability to communicate with healthcare providers, funders, consultants, and other external partners with professionalism and responsiveness
  • Ability to collaborate well with others, including articulating your ideas clearly, whether orally or in writing
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and manage one’s own workload in a remote, self-directed environment
  • Strong desire to work in a group that prioritizes open communication, work-life balance, personal health, and positive relationships

The skills listed above are comprehensive, and we understand that there are great candidates who possess only a subset of those skills, or who have other important skills. If you match some of these skills, please do not hesitate to apply

BENEFITS

Health and Welfare Benefits

  • Comprehensive medical, dental and vision insurance coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts for transportation-related, healthcare and dependent care expenses
  • Employee Assistance Program

For Your Financial Future

  • Life Insurance, Disability Insurance, and Legal Insurance
  • University of California Retirement Plan (a defined benefit plan)
  • Deferred Compensation Plans/Pre-tax Retirement Savings Programs

For Your Work/Life Balance

  • Fifteen paid holidays per year
  • Generous vacation and sick leave

THE HIRING PROCESS

We aim to be transparent and efficient in our hiring process. Applications are reviewed by members of WorkLife Law’s team. Application review will begin December 1, 2026.

Interested candidates should submit the following materials with their application:

  • Resume
  • Cover letter explaining your interest in WorkLife Law and this position

This hiring process will include two video interviews and a skills assessment. In each interview, you will be asked to provide examples of these skills and experiences or how you would draw on your experiences to handle a scenario commonly found at WorkLife Law.

WorkLife Law is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from members of underrepresented communities and are eager to provide disability accommodations, when needed.

Please note: This position has been designated as “sensitive” and requires a pre-employment background check.

Federal law requires employers to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities. Please contact Human Resources if you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job. Examples of reasonable accommodation include making a change to the application process, providing documents in an alternate format, using a sign language interpreter, or using specialized equipment

WHAT TO EXPECT

Applicants who meet the position requirements will be competitively evaluated to identify the individuals whose breadth and depth of experience and education most closely relate to the stated requirements and the needs of the College. Not all applicants will be contacted for an interview.

UC Law San Francisco is an Equal Opportunity Employer. UC Law San Francisco strives to provide a diverse and inclusive educational environment that fosters cultural awareness, mutual understanding and respect. UC Law San Francisco College of the Law is interested in candidates who will contribute to diversity and equal opportunity in higher education through their teaching. Qualified women and members of underrepresented minority groups are strongly encouraged to apply.

Salary: $75,000 – $85,000 / year

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are Finance leaders choose Billtrust to get paid faster, control costs, and maximize customer satisfaction.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Finance leaders choose Billtrust to get paid faster, control costs, and maximize customer satisfaction. As the leader in B2B accounts receivable workflow and payment software, we provide the world’s leading brands with AI-powered solutions across the full AR lifecycle—from invoice presentment and payment processing to cash application and collections. With over 2,600 global customers, more than $1 trillion in invoice dollars processed, and a proprietary network of 13 million buyers, Billtrust delivers business value through deep industry expertise and a culture relentlessly focused on meaningful customer outcomes.

We’re an AI-first company, not just in what we build for our customers, but in how we work. Across every function, our teams use AI tools daily to work faster, make better decisions, and deliver higher-quality outcomes. We hire exceptional people, give them cutting-edge AI capabilities, and measure success by the impact they create. If you want to do the best work of your career at the frontier of AI and fintech, Billtrust is the place to do it.

Our Values

Customers

We relentlessly increase value for customer and do the right thing for them.

Action

We make ‘thoughtfully fast’ decisions, act quickly, cut through red tape, deliver progress not perfection, take ownership and accountability.

Team Spirit

We put the team ahead of ourselves, foster trust and respect, collaborate with passion, despise toxic politics, value our differences, and celebrate together.

Innovation

We challenge the status quo, experiment thoughtfully, and are novel and brilliant in what we create.

Excellence

We love to win, but we hate losing even more. We aspire to be the best and take pride in our work. When we fall short, we own it and come back stronger.

About the Role

The Lead UX Designer is a critical role responsible for setting the standard for design quality, craft, and research rigor across the team. You will leverage AI tools and agents to explore concepts faster, generate design variations, and shorten the path to validation, focusing your expertise on framing the right problems, reading what users need, and deciding what is worth building.

You will own complex problem spaces from framing the opportunity and validating hypotheses with users through to production ready designs across web and platform experiences. That includes designing products with AI features, such as conversational interfaces, predictive UI, AI error and confidence states, and handoffs between people and AI. You think in systems, lead through influence, and do your best work where design decisions have real commercial consequences.

What You’ll Do

Design Leadership & Execution

  • Drive end to end design for complex, multistep SaaS products, from early problem framing through high fidelity prototyping and handoff.
  • Lead the creation of cross platform user flows, interaction models, and design specifications that translate cleanly to engineering.
  • Design AI native product experiences, including conversational UI, predictive features, AI output states, and human and AI interaction patterns, with the same rigor you apply to any other product surface.
  • Use AI design tools and agentic workflows to accelerate exploration, generate design variations, and reduce time to validation.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Research & Insight

  • Plan and run generative and evaluative user research to continuously inform product direction.
  • Synthesize usability studies, analytics, customer feedback, and market analysis into clear design recommendations.
  • Pull your own data in tools like Amplitude or Mixpanel, form hypotheses, and connect design decisions to measurable outcomes.
  • Find friction and opportunity in existing experiences and drive improvements backed by evidence, not assumptions.

Strategy & Influence

  • Frame design problems clearly, connecting user needs to business outcomes and technical constraints.
  • Contribute to product strategy and push back constructively when a proposed solution does not serve users or undermines long term product integrity.
  • Partner with product, engineering, and stakeholders from design through delivery.
  • Contribute to and maintain the team’s design system so the product stays consistent and scalable.

Mentorship & Team Development

  • Mentor and coach junior and mid level designers with structured, actionable feedback on their work and process.
  • Model how to use AI tools thoughtfully in a design workflow, as a multiplier for quality and speed rather than a shortcut.
  • Help shape team processes, critique culture, and design standards, and raise the bar on craft, consistency, and usability.

What You’ll Bring

Required Skills:

  • 8+ years of experience in product design, with demonstrated progression into a lead or senior individual contributor role.
  • Portfolio showing end to end ownership of complex B2B or enterprise SaaS product design, with design thinking and not just visual execution.
  • Deep proficiency in Figma, including component libraries, auto layout, and prototyping.
  • Hands on experience building, scaling, and governing design systems.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are Flow Pouch is a US DTC brand.  We make pouches with no nicotine and no caffeine, sold subscription-first.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Flow Pouch is a US DTC brand. We make pouches with no nicotine and no caffeine, sold subscription-first. We launched in 2024, we have grown quickly, and we are a remote team spread across the US, Europe and Latin America.

Why we are hiring

We are a team of contractors in several countries, and the people side has been run by one person alongside recruiting. As the team grows, we want someone who owns the day-to-day of people operations end to end: contracts, onboarding, the HR system, the monthly payment prep, and a steady flow of candidates for the roles we hire again and again. We are moving to Rippling and building our people records properly from the start, so whoever takes this seat will set up a lot of it for the first time.

What you will own

  • Contracts and documents. Contractor agreements and NDAs from our templates, e-signature, and a filing system where every signed document is findable in seconds.

  • Onboarding and offboarding. Accounts, access, welcome flow, first-week check-ins, clean exits.

  • The HR system. Administration of Rippling: accurate roster data (roles, rates, start dates, locations), the compliance checklist, and the reports the founders need.

  • Monthly payment prep. Collect invoices, check each against the roster and the agreed rate, prepare the payment sheet for one-click approval.

  • Recruiting for recurring roles. Continuous LinkedIn sourcing for video editors, static designers and creative strategist, first screening interviews in English, scheduling with the founders and leads.

  • People records. A records set that would pass a due diligence review tomorrow.

What this role is not

This is not a senior HR role and not an HR business partner seat. Policy, compensation decisions, offers and anything with legal weight stay with the Head of People Ops and the founders. It is not a finance role either: you prepare payments, finance approves and pays. And it is not a full-time recruiter seat: sourcing is about half of your week, the rest is operations.

Who we are looking for

  • You have at least a year in People Ops, HR or recruiting, ideally at a US or DTC company, an ecommerce brand or an agency serving them. This is a junior seat with room to grow.

  • Your English is fluent, spoken and written. You will run screening interviews in English and write to US colleagues every day.

  • Ideally you have some exposure to hiring creative roles: video editors, designers or creative strategists. If you have sourced or screened them, tell us.

  • Ideally you have experience with Rippling. Hands-on time in a similar platform (Deel, BambooHR, HiBob, Personio) also works.

  • You use AI daily and are comfortable with it: drafting, research, checking documents, small automations for your own work.

  • You are comfortable with contractor agreements, spreadsheets and checking numbers carefully, and you are discreet with personal data.

  • You are organised and happy owning admin that others find boring.

What is hard about this

We would rather you hear it now than in month three:

  • A lot of this does not exist yet. You will build the first version of the filing system, the checklists and the roster, not inherit them.

  • Volume comes in waves. A hiring push can mean fifty profiles to screen in a week on top of the regular work.

  • The team is spread across time zones. Some of your afternoons will overlap with US mornings, and you will often be the first to answer a question.

  • Mistakes in this seat are visible. A wrong rate on a payment sheet or a missing contract is noticed by the founders. Care matters more than speed.

The engagement

Type

Full-time, contractor agreement.

Compensation

$2,000 to $2,500 per month depending on experience, paid in USD.

Location

Europe.

Reports to

Head of People Operations & Talent Acquisition.

Start

December 2026.

How to apply

Send us your CV or LinkedIn profile, plus short answers to three questions:

  1. Which HRIS or contractor platforms have you administered, and what did you own in them?

  2. Have you sourced candidates on LinkedIn? If yes, for which roles, and roughly how many hires came from your sourcing?

  3. How do you use AI in your work today? Give one concrete example from the last month.

jobs.excerpt: Title: Threat and Vulnerability Management Analyst Reporting to: Product and Offensive Security Manager The bright side of mortgages nesto is Canada's leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get-go – with total transparency and no haggling.
jobs.description:
Title: Threat and Vulnerability Management Analyst
Reporting to: Product and Offensive Security Manager

The bright side of mortgages

nesto is Canada's leading digital residential mortgage lender, offering Canadians the lowest rates from the get-go – with total transparency and no haggling.

About Us

As Canada's pioneer in online mortgage lending, nesto is transforming the way Canadians finance their homes. Our mission is to offer a positive, empowering, and transparent property financing experience, simplified from start to finish.

Borrowers benefit from rates that are often lower than those offered by the big banks, along with an exceptional end-to-end mortgage experience powered by best-in-class AI technology. Fast, simple, and fully digital, nesto has been recognized as CLA Lender of the Year for three consecutive years. That's the bright side of mortgages.

Nesto Group

Nesto Group is Canada's leading provider of mortgage technology and financing solutions, with more than CAD $80 billion in residential and commercial mortgages under administration. Trusted by many of the country's leading financial institutions, we combine over 50 years of mortgage expertise with proprietary cloud and AI technology to transform the future of lending.

Powered by our proprietary cloud and AI technology, nesto has become one of Canada's fastest-growing mortgage lenders, gaining market share across direct-to-consumer (D2C) residential lending, the broker channel, and multi-family commercial lending. Recognized as one of Deloitte's Fast 50 companies for three consecutive years, we continue to push the industry forward through innovation, technology, and customer-focused solutions.

Operating through our family of brands – CMLS, nesto, and Nesto Cloud – our mission is to build Canada's mortgage ecosystem of the future and create a true Canadian champion in lending technology and financial services.

Work Location

This is a remote-first role open to candidates anywhere in Canada. You'll have the flexibility to work from home or from any of our offices nationwide.

Why We Are Hiring

Vulnerabilities are being weaponized faster than ever. With AI, the gap between a public disclosure and a working exploit has shrunk from weeks to roughly a day, which means threat exposure needs a daily watch. This new role exists so that someone owns it full time: spotting emerging vulnerabilities inside that tight window, working out what they mean for nesto, and getting the right teams to fix what matters.

Just as important is cutting through the noise. There is a lot of it, and our teams should only spend their time on what is worth it. You'll be the person who can explain clearly what is important and what is not.

What You'll Be Doing

1. Continuous, validated watch of the external perimeter

  • Monitor external attack surface management.
  • Test/validate exploitability and reachability of high-impact findings.
  • Challenge results from tools: flag false positives, stale findings and misattributed assets, and feed them back into tool tuning.
  • Own follow-up to closure: assign an owner, track severity-based SLAs, escalate slips, re-test fixes.
  • Explain risk clearly to internal teams and drive remediation.
  • Partner with engineers on fixes, which are largely handled as infrastructure as code, so you can contribute directly to the solution.
  • Keep the external asset inventory accurate: detect shadow and orphaned assets.
  • Report to leadership: open exposure by severity and age, validated-exploitable count, SLA compliance, time to remediate.

2. Threat intelligence watch

  • Monitor threat intel daily for issues that could impact nesto.
  • For each relevant advisory, publish a fast verdict (exposed and exploitable?) with evidence and a recommended action.
  • Prioritize on real-world risk, not CVSS alone.
  • Turn recurring patterns into new checks, watchlists and threat-model input.

3. Tooling and automation, continuous improvement

  • Use AI tooling in your daily workflow to move faster.
  • Finetune Automation: ASM sources, threat enrichment, reachability checks, ticketing, owner notification, SLA tracking, re-testing.
  • Propose tooling improvements from observed gaps (coverage, false positives, enrichment, reporting).
  • Detects new exposure proactively (DNS, certificate transparency, cloud and deployment changes) before it is scanned or exploited.
  • Build reusable validation checks and playbooks others can run.
  • Follow and refine documented procedures to make sure every vulnerability is tracked through to resolution, including the routine steps.
  • Report posture: share of findings handled without manual work, time to detection, time to validated verdict, false-positive rate.

What You Bring

  • 1–3 years of experience in vulnerability management, or equivalent experience in offensive and defensive security.
  • Hands-on experience with attack surface management and vulnerability scanning tools (e.g., Wiz, Nuclei/Neo, or equivalent), including triaging findings by real-world risk and validating exploitability.
  • Experience working in a corporate environment: opening tickets, communicating across teams, and following up until something is resolved.
  • Enough offensive understanding to judge whether a vulnerability is actually exploitable or just noise.
  • A procedural, autonomous way of working: you follow a process through to the end, including the less exciting steps.
  • Strong judgment and research skills, with the curiosity and attention to detail to spot gaps.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with technical and non-technical teams.
  • A healthy skepticism toward AI-generated output: you verify it rather than accept it as given.

Nice-to-Have

  • A background in IT or engineering (not required).
  • Certifications such as OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional) or OSWE (Offensive Security Web Expert), or a recent AI-focused security certification.
  • French is an asset.

This Role Might Be for You If

  • You enjoy structure: finding the vulnerability is only the start for you, and you like seeing it through to the fix.
  • You read a new security advisory and immediately ask "what do we run that this could affect?"
  • When an AI tool gives you an answer, your first instinct is to check it.
  • You are curious enough to keep up with a field that changes daily.
  • You want to help fix problems, not just report them.

Interview Process

  • Recruiter Screen (30 min): A quick intro call to learn about your background and give you a real picture of the role.

Overview

LMI is seeking a Business / Implementation Analyst Lead to support a prospective VA OSP program, contingent upon contract award. This full-time key-personnel role turns human-centered discovery and operating evidence into practical assessment standards, implementation requirements, improvement pathways, and executive decision-support products.

The lead will manage a repeatable process for understanding organizational capacity and implementation conditions, including evidence collection, gap analysis, maturity judgments, prioritization, and reassessment. The work requires careful distinction among issues suitable for technical assistance, program management, data/tool improvements, or government-level decisions.

This position works closely with HCD, evaluation, public-health, data, and project-management personnel. Strong candidates are rigorous analysts who can define workable processes, guide a team of practitioners, and make nuanced organizational findings clear, traceable, and useful.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities

  • Lead business and implementation analysis for the assessment-to-action framework, maturity rubric, and assessment operating procedures.
  • Translate stakeholder interviews and discovery findings into workflow maps, process models, business requirements, and documented decision rules.
  • Develop templates, evidence standards, quality controls, and consistent review practices for initial and recurring organizational assessments.
  • Guide analysts in diagnosing staffing, governance, workflow, partnership, data, and implementation gaps from qualitative and quantitative evidence.
  • Oversee practical, prioritized capacity improvement plans that connect current conditions to next-state goals and observable evidence of progress.
  • Design and sustain a closed-loop process linking findings, routing recommendations, authorized support actions, monitoring, and reassessment.
  • Distinguish contractor analysis and recommendations from policy, grant-management, and other decisions reserved for government personnel.

  • Quality-review findings, improvement plans, process documentation, and decision-ready briefs for consistency and accessibility.

  • Experience coaching analysts, setting review standards, resolving inconsistent assessment conclusions, and producing client-ready decision documentation.
  • Proficiency with Excel, Visio, PowerPoint, SharePoint or comparable Microsoft 365 and process-mapping tools in distributed teams.
  • Experience developing business analysis standards, analyst playbooks, decision matrices, and review procedures that remain usable across different staff, cohorts, and operational settings.
  • Ability to lead structured root-cause and impact analysis while differentiating implementable contractor recommendations from grant-management or policy decisions reserved to government officials.

Desired:

  • Highly desirable: Experience supporting grantee management through evidence reviews, capacity assessments, grant-recipient improvement plans, and technical-assistance routing recommendations.
  • Experience establishing organizational maturity models, readiness assessments, or continuous-improvement programs.
  • CBAP, Lean Six Sigma, or equivalent business/organizational analysis training.

jobs.excerpt: About MISUMI Americas MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions.
jobs.description:
About MISUMI Americas

MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.

MISUMI Americas serves customers through regional sourcing teams and a network of QCTs (warehouses) that hold inventory close to demand. As the business grows, we need one clear, trusted process that connects what sales expects to sell with what we source, build and stock. This role creates and owns that process.

The Director, SIOP is the practice lead for Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning. Each month, they bring together a top-down view (business plan, targets, market signals) and a bottom-up view (account and regional forecasts) over a rolling horizon of six months or more. They turn that consensus demand into requirements by region and into the inventory each QCT must hold. Where supply cannot meet demand, they make the gap visible, size the impact on customer service and revenue, and consolidate the proposed fixes into clear investment options for the executive team.

The Director, SIOP is a peer of the Directors, Portfolio Management and works with them as partners. Portfolio Management owns what we offer: assortment, pricing, launches, exits and supplier capability. SIOP owns how much, where and when: consensus demand, regional supply requirements, QCT inventory targets and the monthly planning process. Phase 1 covers standard and configurable products and QCT inventory; custom process lines are covered through demand and partner-capacity visibility.

This is a Director role with a player-coach start: the person runs the process hands-on at first, then builds a small, highly capable team of planners and analysts. Success is measured by forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns.

  • Own the monthly SIOP cycle: Design, run and keep improving the monthly process end to end: data refresh, demand review, supply review, reconciliation and the executive SIOP meeting. Set the calendar, the inputs each team owes and the decisions each step must produce.
  • Own the consensus demand number: Combine the business plan and targets with account and regional forecasts from Sales and the category overlay from each Portfolio Manager (launches, price changes, exits, competitive moves). Reconcile the views, explain the gaps and agree one demand plan over a rolling horizon of six months or more. Sales owns the account forecast; Portfolio Managers own the assumptions in their overlay; SIOP owns the process and the final number.
  • Translate demand into regional requirements: Map the consensus forecast to supply requirements by region, so regional sourcing teams know what volume and mix they must secure, and when.
  • Set inventory policy and QCT targets: Define safety stock, reorder logic and stocking depth by QCT and SKU class, to meet the service levels agreed in the executive SIOP review within the working-capital envelope set by Finance. Portfolio Managers decide which items are in the stocked set; SIOP decides how deep and where. Plan the run-down of items Portfolio Management decides to exit.
  • Run the input scorecard: Track whether Sales, Portfolio Management and Sourcing deliver complete, on-time and credible inputs each month, and publish the scorecard. The VP, Portfolio Management is the executive sponsor, chairs the monthly review and escalates late or weak Portfolio Management inputs. Late or weak Sales inputs escalate to the executive leadership team through the scorecard. The SVP, Operations & Supply Chain co-sponsors the supply-side inputs (Sourcing and QCTs) and escalates those.
  • Find and size supply and demand mismatches: Identify where demand will exceed supply or capacity, or where we hold inventory that demand does not support. Quantify revenue at risk and service impact. The relevant Portfolio Manager proposes the fix for their category or process; SIOP consolidates the proposals into the executive pre-read.
  • Lead the executive SIOP review: Prepare a concise monthly pre-read and run the executive meeting. Frame the decisions needed (investment, allocation, stocking, capacity), record what was decided and follow up on actions to closure.
  • Own the planning metrics: Define, measure and report forecast accuracy, capacity utilization and, as the practice matures, inventory turns. Set targets with the executive team and drive improvement over time.
  • Build the tools and data foundation: Work with Finance, Business Systems and Data teams to establish the planning data model, forecast history and dashboards the process needs. Choose and implement planning tools as the practice scales.
  • Build the team: Hire, develop and lead a small, high-performing team of demand and supply planners or analysts as the practice grows.

All employees are expected to maintain and contribute to the QMS.

Required

  • Experience: 10+ years in demand planning, supply planning, S&OP / IBP or supply chain operations, with at least 3–5 years leading the S&OP or SIOP process for a multi-region business.
  • Built a process before: A track record of designing and launching a monthly S&OP / SIOP cycle (not only taking part in one), and making it stick across sales, operations and finance.
  • Strong analytical skills: Fluent in forecasting methods, inventory policy (safety stock, service levels, reorder points) and capacity planning. Advanced Excel / Google Sheets; comfortable with BI tools and large data sets.
  • Influence without authority: Proven ability to hold sales and operations leaders accountable for inputs and commitments they do not report to you for.
  • Works as a peer of category owners: Gets the commercial story from category owners and stays out of assortment and pricing decisions.
  • Executive communication: Can turn complex planning data into a short, clear story with options and trade-offs for senior leaders.
  • Business judgment: Can build an investment case that links inventory and capacity decisions to service levels, revenue and working capital.
  • Leadership: Experience hiring and developing planners or analysts, or a strong readiness to build a team from scratch.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations, engineering, business or a related field.

Preferred

  • Industry: Experience in industrial distribution, manufacturing, configurable components or a high-SKU, make-to-order and stock business.
  • Network inventory: Experience setting inventory policy across a network of warehouses or distribution centers.
  • Planning tools: Hands-on experience with planning platforms (for example, Kinaxis, o9, Anaplan, SAP IBP or similar) and ERP data.
  • Global and matrixed work: Experience in a multinational company, including work with a parent company or stakeholders across cultures and time zones.
  • Certification: APICS / ASCM (CPIM or CSCP) or similar is a plus; an MBA or advanced degree is a plus.

AI and automation: Interest in using AI and automation to improve forecasting and reduce manual planning work.

Primarily remote, computer-based work, including extended periods at a computer and on video calls. Occasional visits to QCT (warehouse) and supplier sites, which involve walking, standing and following site safety rules.

Ability to travel up to 20% annually, mainly within the Americas, for QCT and regional sourcing visits, team meetings and offsites, with occasional international travel to work with MISUMI Group planning teams.

Benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Comprehensive medical and dental coverage
  • 401(k) plan
  • Generous PTO and leave programs

Salary Range: $194,360 - $245,220 per year; based upon experience

  • Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
  • Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
  • Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
  • Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.

Must-Haves

Nice to Have

What you'll be doing:

Candidate Scheduling and Experience (~55%)

  • End-to-end scheduling: Coordinate complex, multi-stage, multi-interviewer onsites and remote panels in Ashby across teams and time zones
  • Error-free execution: Own the details that make loops run cleanly, including correct interviewer assignments, accurate invites and links, and clear role-specific instructions for every candidate and interviewer

AI and Automation (Woven Throughout)

  • Design and modify structures, equipment, and interior fittings for rail vehicles, including component layouts, supporting brackets, and fastening systems in compliance with standards and project requirements.
  • Create bolted, welded, and sheet metal assemblies using various materials (steel, stainless steel, aluminum), and develop sheet metal patterns/models.
  • Design plastic and composite components and select hardware items per engineering direction.
  • Prepare material lists and produce detailed drawings for modification, manufacturing, assembly, and installation.
  • Develop assembly manuals and installation instructions.
  • Conduct dimensional surveys on-site or in the workshop to support manufacturing and installation.

Profile/Skills

Education: College diploma (DEC) in mechanical design or Bachelor's degree in Engineering.

Years of experience: 5-10 years experience in metal fabrication and mechanical design, including significant experience with Inventor or Solidworks 3D modeling software (Relevant experience with other modeling software may be considered equivalent).

Technical skills:

  • Proficient in 3D CAD design and drafting, specifically with SolidWorks, including the creation of detailed drawings and flat patterns for rail vehicle components.
  • Strong understanding of materials (metals, plastics, composites) and mechanical assembly methods (bolted, welded, sheet metal).
  • Capable of layout optimization and integration of components according to standards and project requirements.
  • Skilled in preparing material lists, technical documentation, and installation instructions.

Personal and soft skills:

  • Effective problem-solver, adaptable to changing requirements.

*Reasons for requiring bilingualism: You will have the opportunity to work with a varied clientele, including both French- and English-speaking companies. Bilingualism is therefore fundamental to building strong relationships with our customers, understanding their specific needs, communicating effectively in their preferred language and facilitating strategic meetings.

jobs.description:
Remote (US-based, Pacific hours) · Full-time, embedded with a client team · $105,000 to $125,000 annually, DOE

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

About Red Door Collaborative

Red Door Collaborative is a creative agency serving enterprise tech organizations and SMBs with visual design, content, motion, and video work. We're a small, human-centered team: highly collaborative, quietly intense, and genuinely good at what we do. We're also evolving. AI is reshaping our industry, and we're leaning into it as a tool that enhances our work rather than replaces the people doing it.

We're rooted in SoCal and the PNW, but we're a fully remote team of creatives. We work Pacific hours and meet in person rarely. This is a real remote role, not a "remote for now" situation. This role requires someone who can earn a client team's trust from a distance, running its business rhythm over Microsoft Teams, keeping trackers current without being asked, and building decks that leadership can present as they are.

About the Role

We're hiring a Project Marketing Manager to join our embedded team supporting the small and medium business marketing organization of a Fortune 100 enterprise cloud and AI company. You'll be a Red Door employee, working day to day inside the client's marketing team.

This is an execution role with real autonomy. The client team's leadership sets direction, and you take it from there: tracking go-to-market plans, running the team's rhythm of business, building communication decks, and delivering projects for senior leadership without needing a check-in at every step.

You'll report to our Senior Account Manager. We're also hiring a Senior Project Marketing Manager for this team. If you've owned marketing programs end to end for several years, that posting is likely the better fit.

What You'll Do

  • Go-to-market tracking: Own the trackers for the team's go-to-market work: launches, campaigns, and milestones. Keep owners, dates, and status current, and flag risk before it becomes a missed date.
  • Rhythm of business: Run the team's operating cadence, from recurring business reviews to planning cycles and status meetings. Prepare agendas, pull the inputs, capture decisions and action items, and follow through on them.
  • Communication decks: Build PowerPoint decks for leadership reviews, team updates, and stakeholder communication. Turn raw inputs and data into a clear story that leaders can present as is.
  • Projects for senior leadership: Take on projects assigned by senior leadership and deliver them end to end, from clarifying the ask to handing over the finished work.

Who You Are

  • Enterprise marketing experience: You have 4+ years of professional marketing experience with enterprise organizations, in program, project, or marketing operations work. Agency or vendor-side experience embedded with an enterprise client counts.
  • PowerPoint and deck building: You build decks regularly, and leaders use them. You can take scattered inputs and shape them into a clear, well-designed story.
  • Autonomy: You take direction from leadership, then run with it. You don't need step-by-step instructions, and you know when a check-in is worth someone's time.
  • Operational follow-through: Trackers stay current and meetings end with clear owners because you make it a practice, not because someone reminds you.
  • AI-forward: Red Door is an AI-forward agency. You understand the value AI brings to marketing work, you already use it in your own work, and you go looking for new and better ways to put it to use.

Before You Apply

Consider the following before applying:

  • If your marketing experience is mostly outside of enterprise organizations…
  • If you're more comfortable waiting for detailed instructions than taking a direction and running with it…
  • If building decks and keeping trackers current feels like a chore rather than the core of the job…
  • If you're looking to set marketing strategy rather than drive its execution…

Then this probably isn't the right role for you.

To Apply

In your cover letter, tell us about a deck you're proud of: who it was for, what it had to accomplish, and what you'd change about it now. We're more interested in how you think about your audience than in the slides themselves.

During the interview process, we may ask you to walk us through a deck or tracker you've built, with any confidential details removed. Finalists will be asked to provide references from people they've worked with directly.

Compensation & Benefits

This is a salaried, exempt position with an annual salary of $105,000 to $125,000, depending on experience.

We offer a full benefits package: PTO (80 hours in your first year, increasing with years of service), paid holidays (11 per year), health coverage (medical, dental, vision, plus HSA/FSA options), 401(k) with match, life and disability insurance, a charitable matching program, and stipends to support your remote setup and ongoing work-from-home costs.

Equal Opportunity

Red Door Collaborative is committed to building an inclusive team where everyone is valued and respected. We don't discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status. We don't just welcome diverse perspectives; we actively seek them out. People from different cultures and experiences, solving problems together, is how we do our best work.

jobs.title: Software Engineer 4 - AI Native
jobs.excerpt: The Company Serving the People Who Serve the People Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together.
jobs.description:
The Company

Serving the People Who Serve the People

Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together. We are on a mission to support our customers with meeting the needs of their communities and implementing our technology in ways that are equitable and inclusive. Granicus has consistently appeared on the GovTech 100 list over the past 5 years and has been recognized as the best companies to work on BuiltIn.

Over the last 25 years, we have served 5,500 federal, state, and local government agencies and more than 300 million citizen subscribers power an unmatched Subscriber Network that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place. With comprehensive cloud-based solutions for communications, government website design, meeting and agenda management software, records management, and digital services, Granicus empowers stronger relationships between government and residents across the U.S., U.K., Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By simplifying interactions with residents, while disseminating critical information, Granicus brings governments closer to the people they serve—driving meaningful change for communities around the globe.

Want to know more? See more of what we do here.

Job Summary

Granicus serves more than 7,000 public-sector agencies and powers approximately 30 billion digital interactions annually. Within the Office of the CTO, we operate an AI-native software development lifecycle: a production engineering model in which autonomous agents perform high-confidence implementation work and senior engineers orchestrate, review, and own the outcome. The model is established and operating; we are scaling it across additional delivery teams.

This role joins one of those teams. Our engineering standards are calibrated to the practices used by leading software and AI organizations — generator-verifier architecture, eval-driven development, staged deployment, and high-volume autonomous pull-request pipelines — operated within a FedRAMP-authorized environment. We are hiring practitioners who will set and uphold these standards, not engineers who simply use AI tooling.

Operating constraints (non-negotiable): agents execute only within branches; all agent-generated code passes senior human review before merging to production; autonomous execution is a force multiplier and does not transfer accountability away from the responsible engineer. Compliance obligations — NIST 800-53 Rev 5, WCAG, SOC 2, and applicable FedRAMP authorizations — are treated as engineering requirements and a source of competitive advantage.

Why this role exists

When agents produce the majority of initial implementation, the scarce engineering skill shifts from authoring code to directing it, reviewing it rigorously at volume, and owning whether it is correct. This role is for a senior engineer who has made that transition: decomposing work for the agent array, authoring the evaluation suites that hold agent output to a measurable standard, reviewing agent-generated pull requests with greater rigor than most engineers apply to their own work, and shipping production code within a FedRAMP-authorized environment. The role contributes to defining how engineers operate in an AI-native lifecycle, not merely to adopting AI tooling.

What Your Impact Will Look Like

  • Direct the agent array on production workstreams — decompose problems into tasks suitable for agent execution, dispatch them, and integrate the output into shipped software.
  • Review agent-generated pull requests at volume and at depth — identify correctness, security, and accessibility defects that automated tests do not catch, while maintaining review throughput and a consistent quality bar.
  • Author evaluation suites that make quality measurable — define criteria under which the pipeline validates correctness rather than relying on subjective assessment. Eval-driven development is your standard practice.
  • Own quality end to end — correctness, performance, security posture, and WCAG accessibility of the software your team ships, irrespective of which component or agent produced the initial implementation.
  • Advance workstreams along the autonomy ladder on the basis of evidence — move work from supervised to autonomous execution when measured reliability supports it, and revert promptly when it does not.
  • Strengthen the development lifecycle itself — identify where patterns, prompts, or pipeline components degrade at volume and work with the lead architect to remediate them.
  • Maintain agent operations within the security boundary — branch-only execution, vaulted credentials, sandboxed actions, and in-VPC inference. Throughput does not justify exceptions.
  • OWNERSHIP FROM DAY ONE
    • An active workstream directed through the agent array
    • Agent pull-request review as a core, high-signal responsibility
    • Evaluation suites authored and owned for your team’s deliverables
    • End-to-end quality ownership within the FedRAMP-authorized environment

  • SCOPE YOU WILL GROW INTO

    • Higher autonomy ratios substantiated by reliability data
    • Reusable prompt and evaluation patterns adopted by other engineers
    • Contribution to the lifecycle standards as a co-author, not only a user
    • Mentorship of engineers transitioning to agent-directed delivery

You Will Love This Job If You Have

Required

  • Strong engineering fundamentals. Data structures, systems design, and testing, with the ability to read unfamiliar code quickly and assess it accurately. Agents amplify engineering judgment; they do not substitute for it.
  • A record of shipping production software you owned the quality of, including responsibility for diagnosis and remediation when it failed.
  • Hands-on experience directing coding agents on production work, including their failure modes and the practice of reviewing agent-generated code critically rather than approving it by default.
  • Demonstrated code-review competence. You identify defects that automated tests do not catch, provide actionable feedback, and maintain a high bar without becoming a bottleneck.
  • High autonomy. You advance work without step-by-step direction and escalate issues proactively.

Preferred

  • High-assurance or regulated experience. Shipping within FedRAMP, defense, financial services, healthcare, or another NIST 800-53 / SOC 2 / HIPAA-bound environment.
  • Depth in evaluation authoring or test-first development within a rigorous engineering culture.
  • Full-stack range, sufficient to review front-end and back-end agent output with equal confidence.
  • Public-sector or govtech experience and familiarity with the relevant end users.

Indicators of a strong fit

  • You deliver more effectively by directing multiple agents than by authoring code directly, while retaining a precise understanding of the intended implementation.
  • You regard rigorous code review as a core engineering competency.
  • You prefer to establish quality through evaluation suites rather than through discussion.
  • You treat the agent array as leverage and reliably identify when its output is incorrect.
  • You want to contribute to how engineering is practiced here, not only to apply new tooling.

Indicators this role is not a fit

  • You measure your contribution by lines of code personally authored. That metric does not apply in this model.
  • You approve pull requests without thorough review under time pressure. At agent volume, this is the primary path by which defects reach production.
  • You are uncomfortable owning quality for code you did not author. Ownership here is intentionally decoupled from authorship.
  • You regard evaluation and compliance as impediments to shipping.
  • You prefer narrowly scoped tickets and no involvement in how the system operates.

Pay Range

USD $88,000.00 - USD $180,000.00 /Yr.

About Us

Don’t have all the skills/experience mentioned above? At Granicus, we are trying to build diverse, inclusive teams. We do not have degree requirements for most of our roles. If you don’t meet every requirement above but are excited to learn more, we encourage you to apply. We might just be able to find another role that could be a perfect fit!

Security and Privacy Requirements

  • Responsible for Granicus information security by appropriately preserving the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of Granicus information assets in accordance with the company's information security program.
  • Responsible for ensuring the data privacy of our employees and customers, their data, as well as taking all required privacy training in a timely manner, in accordance with company policies.

The Team

  • We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed workforce across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, India, Armenia, Australia, and New Zealand.

The Culture

  • At Granicus, we are building a transparent, inclusive, and safe space for everyone who wants to bea part of our journey.
  • A few culture highlights include – Employee Resource Groups to encourage diverse voices
  • Coffee with Mark sessions – Our employees get to interact with our CEO on very important andsometimes difficult issues ranging from mental health to work-life balance and current affairs.
  • Microsoft Teams communities focused on wellness, art, furbabies, family, parenting, and more.
  • We bring in special guests from time to time to discuss issues that impact our employeepopulation

The Impact

  • We are proud to serve dynamic organizations around the globe that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place — quite literally. We have so many powerful success stories that illustrate how our solutions are impacting the world. See more of our impact here.

The Benefits

At Granicus, we offer a comprehensive and flexible benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance—starting from day one. Here’s what you can expect as a U.S.-based team member:

Flexibility & Balance

  • Flexible Time Off – Take the time you need to rest, recharge, and live your life.
  • Company-Wide Wellbeing Days – Paid days off to unplug and focus on your mental health.
  • Work From Home Reimbursement – Support a productive home office environment.
Health & Wellness
  • Multiple Health Plan Options – Including a 100% employer-paid plan.
  • Employer HSA Contributions – When enrolled in a High-Deductible Health Plan.
  • Fitness Reimbursement Program – Stay active, your way.
  • On-Demand Mental Health Support – Access to Headspace and other wellness tools.
Family & Future
  • Paid Parental Leave – For both birthing and non-birthing parents.
  • Traditional & Roth 401(k) – With a generous company match.
  • Life & AD&D Insurance – 100% employer-paid coverage for peace of mind.
Growth & Recognition
  • Online Learning Platforms – Fuel your professional development.
  • Competitive Salary & Bonuses – Your contributions are valued and rewarded.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Granicus is committed to providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants and employees will be considered for employment and advancement without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, physical or mental disability, age, genetic information, sexual or affectional orientation, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, familial status, military or veteran status or any other status protected by applicable law.

jobs.excerpt: Cos'è Blox Space?  Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia Bitcoin, in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo del fintech, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro.
jobs.description:
Cos'è Blox Space?

Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia Bitcoin, in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo del fintech, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro. Aiutiamo a connettere i talenti con l'ecosistema Bitcoin, operando come Talent Bridge tra le ambizioni di crescita dei professionisti e le opportunità offerte dal nostro network. In questo momento stiamo supportando una delle nostre partner companies nella ricerca di un Senior Growth Marketer (SEO & GEO), e se pensi di essere il profilo giusto, ci piacerebbe conoscerti.

L'azienda e il ruolo

L'azienda è uno dei nomi storici del Bitcoin applicato ai pagamenti, attiva da oltre dieci anni, con più di un milione di clienti in oltre 180 paesi e un team distribuito su più di 30 paesi. Cerchiamo un Senior Growth Marketer che la renda la risposta di default su tre canali: SEO programmatica, app store e motori di risposta AI. È un ruolo con ampia libertà: quali pagine costruire su larga scala, quali esperimenti lanciare e come rendere il sito leggibile dalle macchine. Non cerchiamo il curriculum perfetto, cerchiamo la testa giusta. Cerchiamo chi fa crescere i numeri organici per davvero e sa muoversi dove la ricerca sta andando, dai motori classici all'AI. Le responsabilità di un Senior Growth Marketer in questo contesto possono spaziare dalla proprietà della crescita organica su search, app store e AI, alla costruzione e allo scaling della SEO programmatica (individuare i tipi di pagina che valgono, poi pubblicare, misurare e iterare), dall'ottimizzazione delle schede iOS e Android insieme a prodotto e design al farsi citare nelle risposte di ChatGPT, Perplexity e Google AI Overviews, fino a rendere il sito facile da trovare e da usare per gli agenti AI (dati strutturati, pagine machine-readable, agentic commerce), scrivendo e plasmando i contenuti e mettendo mano al front-end quando è più veloce che aspettare un ticket.

Le skill che fanno la differenza

  • 5+ anni in growth, SEO o performance marketing, con un track record di numeri organici fatti crescere davvero.
  • SEO programmatica e tecnica, hands-on: hai costruito pagine su larga scala e sai renderle efficaci.
  • Lavoro su GEO / AI visibility, con risultati dimostrabili: farsi trovare dai motori di risposta AI è già parte del tuo mestiere.
  • Uso quotidiano di strumenti AI (requisito non negoziabile): Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor o simili. Su questo non transigiamo.
  • A tuo agio con le basi di front-end (un po' di React è un plus), bravo a scrivere e con un buon occhio per il design.
  • Data-driven e autonomo: leggi Search Console e analytics da vicino, e porti avanti le opportunità senza aspettare una roadmap.
  • Sono VERY Nice to Have: esperienza ASO hands-on su iOS e Android, dimestichezza con dati strutturati, llms.txt o API e MCP agent-facing, essere crypto-native, SEO e-commerce o marketplace su cataloghi grandi, o skill Figma per asset e landing page.

Ti manca qualcosa rispetto a quello che hai letto? Candidati comunque: siamo a caccia di game-changer, non di checklist da spuntare!

Work arrangements

Il ruolo ha come sede preferenziale l'hub di Blox Space a Torino, ma è aperto anche a candidature in remoto. L'azienda è remote-first dal primo giorno, con un team distribuito su più di 30 paesi e ritrovi periodici di persona. Se lo desideri puoi essere pagato in crypto.

Unisciti all'ecosistema con Blox Space!

Se vuoi far crescere la presenza organica di un prodotto Bitcoin usato da oltre un milione di persone, dai motori di ricerca all'AI, questa è l'opportunità che stavi aspettando: lavorare con una delle nostre partner companies significa entrare in un team innovativo e in forte crescita, al centro di un ecosistema dove circolano idee, competenze e progetti ad alta intensità. È un ambiente dove si costruisce, si testa, si discute e si migliora ogni giorno.

jobs.title: ME00703-Software Tester (Manual/Automation)
jobs.excerpt: Momentum Engineering, Inc.  fosters an employee-centric culture.
jobs.description:
Momentum Engineering, Inc. fosters an employee-centric culture. Our strength lies in our people. With a high percentage of employees holding advanced degrees in engineering, computer science, and related disciplines, we bring deep technical expertise to every mission. Our team includes professionals with security clearances and full-scope polygraphs, ensuring trusted, secure support for the most sensitive national security initiatives. Additionally, our workforce is equipped with industry-leading certifications, demonstrating a commitment to continuous learning and excellence. Most importantly, our exceptional employee retention rate reflects a culture of professional growth, mission focus, and dedication—ensuring long-term stability and expertise for our customers’ critical needs.

Job Summary

  • Seeking a Mid-level Software Tester responsible for ensuring the quality, functionality, accessibility, and reliability of enterprise web applications through a combination of manual and automated testing
  • The Software Tester will work closely with developers, business analysts, product owners, and fellow testers to validate business requirements, identify defects, and support the successful delivery of software releases
  • This position contributes to all phases of testing, including functional, integration, regression, accessibility, automation, and user acceptance testing
  • This position performs a combination of manual and automated testing where priorities may shift based on release schedules, UAT activities, and program needs
  • The ideal candidate should be comfortable executing detailed manual testing while contributing to the continued growth of the program's Selenium automation suite
  • The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented testing professional with strong manual testing experience and hands-on experience developing and maintaining Selenium-based automation solutions using Java and JUnit
  • This individual will join an established team of Software Engineers, Business Analysts, Project Managers, Solution Architects, Testers, and Cybersecurity professionals supporting a mission-critical Department of Defense application

Primary Responsibilities

  • Test Planning and Execution
    • Analyze business requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and workflows to develop comprehensive test plans and test cases
    • Develop, maintain, and execute manual test plans, test cases, and test scripts
    • Perform functional, integration, regression, user acceptance, accessibility, and compliance testing
    • Prioritize test scenarios based on business impact, risk, and release schedules
    • Execute tests to validate system functionality, performance, and usability
    • Design, prepare, and maintain test data to support testing activities
    • Review test results and evaluate software against business and technical requirements
    • Participate in Agile ceremonies, including daily standups, sprint planning, backlog refinement, and release planning, sprint demos, and retrospectives
    • Learn program mission objectives, business processes, and system architecture to support effective testing
  • Test Automation
    • Design, develop, maintain, and execute automated test scripts using Selenium WebDriver, Java, and JUnit
    • Expand automation coverage by converting manual regression tests into automated scripts
    • Analyze automation results, investigate failures, and work with developers to resolve issues
    • Contribute to the ongoing improvement and maintenance of the automation framework
    • Identify opportunities to improve testing efficiency and expand automation coverage
    • Support future integration of automated testing into GitLab CI/CD pipelines
  • Defect Management and Collaboration
    • Document, track, and retest defects in Jira
    • Collaborate with developers to troubleshoot issues, validate fixes, and ensure resolution
    • Participate in defect triage and support prioritization efforts
    • Communicate testing results, risks, and quality concerns to stakeholders
    • Work closely with developers, DevOps engineers, UI/UX designers, business analysts, and other testers to ensure quality throughout the software development lifecycle
  • Accessibility and Compliance Testing
    • Perform Section 508 accessibility testing using tools such as Axe Monitor and JAWS
    • Validate compliance with accessibility standards and document findings
    • Collaborate with development teams to resolve accessibility issues and improve user experience
    • Support testing to ensure compliance with applicable federal and DoD requirements
  • Process Improvement
    • Contribute to testing standards, methodologies, and process improvement initiatives
    • Help create and maintain testing documentation, user testing guides, and test artifacts
    • Support continuous improvement efforts that enhance software quality, testing effectiveness, and team efficiency
    • Work independently while collaborating effectively in a cross-functional Agile team

Required Qualifications

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a DoD Public Trust clearance or higher
  • At least five years of software quality assurance and testing experience
  • Experience with manual functional, automation, integration, regression, and user acceptance testing
  • Hands-on experience developing and maintaining Selenium WebDriver automated test scripts
  • Proficiency in Java and JUnit
  • Experience creating test plans, test cases, and test scripts from business requirements and user stories
  • Experience using Jira for defect tracking and test management
  • Experience testing web applications
  • Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment with changing deadlines

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with GitLab and CI/CD practices
  • Experience supporting automation initiatives and enhancing test frameworks
  • Experience with API testing tools and methodologies
  • Experience with Section 508 accessibility testing
  • Experience using accessibility testing tools such as Axe Monitor and JAWS
  • Familiarity with SAFe Agile practices
  • Experience supporting DoD, DLA, or other federal government programs
  • Knowledge of security testing and secure software development practices

Exempt hourly position. 11 paid holidays, minimum of 3 weeks PTO, company sponsored group medical plan, company paid dental, vision, life insurance, and STD/LTD plans. Salary is dependent upon the candidate’s experience and qualifications.
