jobs.excerpt: Blink Charging Co.  (Nasdaq: BLNK) is a leading owner, operator, and provider of electric vehicle (EV) charging equipment and networked EV charging services.
jobs.description:
Blink Charging Co. (Nasdaq: BLNK) is a leading owner, operator, and provider of electric vehicle (EV) charging equipment and networked EV charging services. We're on a mission to accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles by deploying thousands of charging stations across the United States and around the world.

What We Do:

Blink offers both residential and commercial EV charging equipment and connectivity to the Blink Network—a comprehensive cloud-based software that operates, manages, and tracks our EV charging stations and payment processing. Our charging solutions serve a diverse range of customers including multi-family residential and commercial properties, airports, colleges, municipalities, parking garages, shopping malls, retail parking, and more.

Why Blink:

  • Industry Leader: We're at the forefront of the EV charging revolution, building critical infrastructure for a sustainable future
  • Innovation-Driven: We continuously develop cutting-edge technology to improve the EV charging experience
  • Growth Opportunity: Join a rapidly expanding company in one of the world's fastest-growing industries
  • Mission That Matters: Every day, we're helping reduce carbon emissions and create a cleaner planet

Position Overview

The Host Support Specialist is a frontline customer support professional responsible for assisting Blink station hosts with operational, technical, account, billing, and general service needs. The role owns customer interactions from initial contact through resolution, completes effective first-line troubleshooting, documents each case accurately, and coordinates with internal teams when additional expertise or action is required.

The successful candidate will combine strong customer care with practical technical aptitude, clear communication, disciplined case management, and consistent follow-through. This role is essential to building host confidence, reducing service disruption, and delivering a professional and responsive customer experience.

Here's What You'll Do:

·Provide timely, professional support to station hosts through inbound and outbound telephone, email, and case-management channels.

·Own support cases from intake through resolution, including diagnosis, documentation, customer updates, internal coordination, escalation, and closure.

·Troubleshoot common EV charging station issues, including connectivity interruptions, charging failures, stations appearing offline, RFID access concerns, and other service-impacting conditions.

·Guide hosts through approved first line troubleshooting steps, such as confirming station status, validating error information, and safely completing a power cycle when appropriate.

·Collect complete diagnostic information before escalation, including station ID, site details, symptoms, error messages, photographs, screenshots, timing, frequency, and business impact.

·Address or route account questions, billing enquiries, reimbursement requests, user-access issues, and other host service needs in accordance with established procedures.

·Coordinate with Network Operations Centre (NOC), Technical Support, Field Services, Account Management, Finance, and other internal teams to drive timely and sustainable resolution.

·Provide hosts with clear expectations, realistic next steps, and proactive status updates, particularly when resolution depends on another team, vendor, part, or site visit.

·Maintain accurate case notes, contact reasons, categorization, asset information, actions taken, commitments, customer communications, and closure details in the designated CRM or ticketing platform.

·Follow escalation paths, quality standards, knowledge articles, safety requirements, and service-level expectations.

·Identify recurring issues, process gaps, and knowledge needs, and share actionable feedback that improves support quality and operational performance.

·Demonstrate empathy, ownership, and sound judgement in every interaction, including escalated or high-impact customer situations.

What You Bring to the Table:

·2-3 years of experience in customer service, technical support, contact center, help desk, or a comparable customer-facing environment.

·Excellent spoken and written English communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information in clear, customer-friendly language.

·Demonstrated customer service, de-escalation, conflict-resolution, and problem-solving skills.

·Basic technical aptitude and the ability to follow structured troubleshooting and diagnostic processes.

·Experience using a CRM, help desk, or ticketing platform to manage cases and document customer interactions.

·Strong attention to detail, accurate documentation habits, and effective follow-through.

·Ability to manage competing priorities and a high volume of customer contacts while maintaining quality and professionalism.

·Ability to work independently, make sound decisions within defined procedures, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

·Availability to work rotational shifts, including weekends and holidays when required by the business.

Success Measures

Performance will be measured through a balanced set of customer, quality, operational, and case management outcomes, which may include:

·Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) and quality assurance scores.

·First Contact Resolution (FCR) and effective troubleshooting.

·Service-level, response-time, and schedule adherence.

·Case ageing, follow-up discipline, and resolution efficiency.

·Accuracy and completeness of case documentation, categorization, and customer data.

·Average Handle Time (AHT), considered alongside quality, complexity, and customer outcome.

·Professionalism, ownership, teamwork, and contribution to continuous improvement.

jobs.excerpt: Cos'è Blox Space?  Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia Bitcoin, in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo del fintech, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro.
jobs.description:
Cos'è Blox Space?

Blox Space lavora al centro dell'economia Bitcoin, in partnership con un network di oltre 70 realtà attive nel mondo del fintech, della cybersecurity e delle Freedom Technologies, impegnate nello sviluppo di infrastrutture, prodotti e servizi legati all'economia digitale, alla data protection e al futuro del denaro. Aiutiamo a connettere i talenti con l'ecosistema Bitcoin, operando come Talent Bridge tra le ambizioni di crescita dei professionisti e le opportunità offerte dal nostro network. In questo momento stiamo supportando una delle nostre partner companies nella ricerca di un Engineering Manager, e se pensi di essere il profilo giusto, ci piacerebbe conoscerti.

L'azienda e il ruolo

L'azienda è uno dei nomi storici del Bitcoin applicato ai pagamenti, attiva da oltre dieci anni, profittevole fin dal lancio, con più di un milione di clienti in oltre 180 paesi e un team distribuito su più di 30 paesi. Cerchiamo un Engineering Manager che guidi circa 30 ingegneri su più team di prodotto e fusi orari, con un obiettivo chiaro: far sì che 30 ingegneri si muovano come un team solo. Oggi tenere i team allineati, sugli stessi standard e nella stessa direzione ricade sui senior engineer, sopra al loro lavoro: questo ruolo nasce per prenderselo. Non cerchiamo il curriculum perfetto, cerchiamo la testa giusta. Cerchiamo chi dà direzione tecnica senza smettere di scrivere codice, e che sa far crescere le persone. Le responsabilità di un Engineering Manager in questo contesto possono spaziare dal coordinare i team di sviluppo riducendo duplicazioni e attriti nei passaggi di consegna, al dare direzione tecnica mantenendo coerenti standard, processi e strumenti, dal tradurre la strategia di prodotto in direzione concreta per i team allo sbloccare gli ingegneri, fare mentoring e proteggere la cultura tecnica, fino alla gestione di 1:1, crescita di carriera e performance, e al contribuire all'hiring, ripensando i metodi di valutazione alla luce degli strumenti AI.

Le skill che fanno la differenza

  • AI-native nel modo di lavorare (requisito non negoziabile): usi strumenti di AI coding ogni giorno (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor o simili). Su questo non transigiamo.
  • Diversi anni da ingegnere prima del passaggio al management, e scrivi ancora codice: guidi da chi il mestiere lo conosce da dentro.
  • Esperienza nella gestione di ingegneri, idealmente su più di un team: sai tenere insieme gruppi che corrono in parallelo.
  • Solide competenze di system design e dimestichezza con lo stack: Node.js, TypeScript, MongoDB, MySQL, Typesense, AWS, Kubernetes.
  • Esperienza nella gestione di team remoti e nell'hiring di ingegneri.
  • Comunicazione chiara in inglese, con un buon overlap con i fusi orari europei e americani.
  • Sono VERY Nice to Have: essere crypto-native, esperienza in payments o e-commerce, aver costruito un processo di hiring da zero, o aver fatto crescere ingegneri junior in solidi mid-level.

Ti manca qualcosa rispetto a quello che hai letto? Candidati comunque: siamo a caccia di game-changer, non di checklist da spuntare!

Work arrangements

Il ruolo ha come sede preferenziale l'hub di Blox Space a Torino, ma è aperto anche a candidature in remoto. L'azienda è remote-first dal primo giorno, con un team distribuito su più di 30 paesi e ritrovi periodici di persona. Se lo desideri puoi essere pagato in crypto.

Unisciti all'ecosistema con Blox Space!

Se vuoi guidare un team di ingegneri che costruisce pagamenti Bitcoin per oltre un milione di persone, questa è l'opportunità che stavi aspettando: lavorare con una delle nostre partner companies significa entrare in un team innovativo e in forte crescita, al centro di un ecosistema dove circolano idee, competenze e progetti ad alta intensità tecnica. È un ambiente dove si costruisce, si testa, si discute e si migliora ogni giorno.

Kreate is a family-owned plastic injection molding company headquartered in Findlay, Ohio, with operations across five states. We create consumer goods sold by major retailers—products that improve everyday experiences for the people who use them.

What makes Kreate different is how we think. We’re on a mission to reimagine familiar product categories and turn “same old” into “new and improved.” That mindset drives everything we do—from product development and manufacturing to how we invest in our people and run our operations.

Innovation at Kreate isn’t limited to engineering or design teams. It shows up on the plant floor, in continuous improvement efforts, in how we adopt new technologies, and in how we support our teams. We’re always evolving—our processes, our tools, and our capabilities—because we believe the best ideas can come from anywhere.

As a family-owned company, we take a long-term approach to growth. We value accountability, collaboration, and people who take pride in their work. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to make an impact, learn new skills, and help shape how we build products and run our business.

If you’re looking for a place where innovation is expected, initiative is encouraged, and your work truly matters, we’d love to Kreate the future together.

We are seeking an Ecommerce Merchandising Specialist to support and enhance our growing ecommerce presence across major retail platforms, including Home Depot, Amazon, our brand websites and other retailer channels. This role will be responsible for developing, optimizing and maintaining compelling product listings that drive visibility, engagement and sales. The ideal candidate will bring a strong understanding of ecommerce content management, SEO and emerging AI-driven search strategies, with an eye for creating effective product content that strengthens the customer shopping experience.

This position will play an important role in improving product content performance, maintaining accurate product information across platforms, and identifying new opportunities to grow our online assortment. Working cross-functionally with internal teams, designers and retail partners, the Ecommerce Merchandising Specialist will use consumer insights, performance data and testing to guide content improvements and merchandising decisions. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented, digitally savvy professional who enjoys building processes, testing new ideas and helping drive ecommerce growth.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain product pages on Home Depot, Amazon, our brand sites and other retailer .com sites, covering images, video, titles, bullets, descriptions, specifications and enhanced content.
  • Take written product copy (titles, bullets, descriptions) and improve its SEO, AEO, GEO.
  • Measure content effectiveness through test & learn campaigns.
  • Provide best practice direction on product page infographics and lifestyle images.
  • Run review generation through retailer programs such as Home Depot Seeds, Influenster campaigns and other sampling programs, within each platform's rules. Track ratings and review volume on new items to achieve targets.
  • Submit removal requests for reviews that break retailer guidelines, and send product or packaging issues raised in reviews to the right team.
  • Manage retailer support cases, such as listing errors, content updates, item merges and suppressions, and follow each one to resolution.
  • Maintain master product data so attributes, dimensions, UPCs, specifications and image assets match across every retailer and our internal reference.
  • Run consumer surveys and quick-poll tests on concepts, colors, pack sizes and names, and summarize the findings for product teams and leadership.
  • Generate, test and launch online-only assortment and virtual bundles. Validate concepts against search demand and survey data, build the case, and set it up with retailers.
  • Audit listings against our own and our retailer’s content standards on a regular schedule and put fixes in place.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years in ecommerce merchandising, content or catalog management for a consumer products brand or retailer.
  • Working knowledge of SEO and keyword research tools such as Semrush. Understanding of how to influence AI recommendations on retailer sites and off platform.
  • A good eye for product and brand content.
  • Detail-oriented with product data (attributes, UPCs, spec sheets), with strong Excel skills.
  • Comfortable running simple consumer surveys and summarizing results.
  • Eager to learn and build new tools and processes.
  • Communicates clearly with designers, agencies and retailer support teams.
  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Company Details:

This role is operational and administrative in nature. It does not include trust accounting, reconciliations, disbursements, or portfolio-level financial management.

Lease & Agreement Management

Administrative & Systems Management

Compliance & Documentation Tracking

Maintenance & Inspection Coordination

  • Receive and process maintenance requests
  • Dispatch vendors and confirm scheduling

Tenant Communications

  • Respond to tenant inquiries professionally and in a timely manner

Note: The role may submit bills, process estimates, and enter lease and rent data into the system, but all financial reconciliations and monetary oversight remain with management.

Ideal Candidate

You are:

  • Highly organized and deadline-driven
  • Comfortable managing recurring compliance requirements
  • Detail-oriented with strong document accuracy
  • Calm and professional in tenant-facing communication
  • Proactive about tracking renewals, insurance expirations, and inspection cycles
  • Comfortable working independently in a structured, process-based environment
  • Interested in growing with a scaling property management portfolio

jobs.excerpt: Consultor Senior SAP PPM (Gestion de Portafolio y Proyectos) Descripción de la empresa Cliente: Aerolinea Descripción de la vacante Por ahora es revisar la propuesta y avanzar en presentarla.
jobs.description:
Consultor Senior SAP PPM (Gestion de Portafolio y Proyectos)

Descripción de la empresa

Cliente: Aerolinea

Descripción de la vacante

Por ahora es revisar la propuesta y avanzar en presentarla.

Gestión de Portafolio y Proyectos: Es la solución de SAP para administrar los proyectos de una empresa y decidir en cuáles invertir.

PPM especializado en validación de propuestas y estructuración de proyectos de tecnología, Software Factory, SaaS y Transformación Digital.

La relación entre SAP PS (Project System), SAP IM (Investment Management) y SAP PPM (Portfolio and Project Management) radica en cómo una organización planifica, aprueba, ejecuta y controla sus inversiones y proyectos desde el nivel más estratégico hasta el nivel más operativo y contable.
​En términos simples, representan una jerarquía de gestión de arriba hacia abajo (Top-Down) y una consolidación de costos de abajo hacia arriba (Bottom-Up).
​1. El rol de cada módulo en el ecosistema
​SAP PPM (Portfolio and Project Management) – Nivel Estratégico y Táctico:
Es el módulo enfocado en la toma de decisiones y gestión de portafolios. Responde a la pregunta: "¿Qué proyectos deberíamos hacer para cumplir con los objetivos del negocio?". Permite evaluar ideas (iniciativas), priorizar inversiones, analizar riesgos, gestionar capacidad de recursos a alto nivel y hacer seguimiento mediante tableros de control (dashboards).
​SAP IM (Investment Management) – Nivel Financiero y Presupuestario:
Es el puente financiero entre la estrategia y la ejecución. Responde a la pregunta: "¿Cuánto dinero tenemos aprobado para invertir y cómo lo distribuimos?". Gestiona programas de inversión (estructuras jerárquicas de presupuesto CAPEX/OPEX), solicitudes de aprobación de inversión (Appropriation Requests) y la distribución de presupuestos hacia los objetos ejecutores.
​SAP PS (Project System) – Nivel Operativo y Contable:
Es el motor de ejecución y control detallado. Responde a la pregunta: "¿Cómo ejecutamos el proyecto día a día y cuánto nos está costando realmente?". Gestiona la estructura de desglose del trabajo (PEP / WBS), grafos, actividades, tiempos, compras, asignación detallada de materiales/servicios, costos reales, compromisos y la liquidación final hacia activos fijos (AA) o centros de costo (CO).
​2. ¿Cómo se integran y fluyen los datos entre ellos?
​El flujo estándar de extremo a extremo (End-to-End) funciona de la siguiente manera:
​1. Ideación y Selección (SAP PPM):
​Se crea un Ítem de Portafolio (o Iniciativa) en PPM.
​Se evalúa su rentabilidad (VAN, TIR), riesgo y alineación estratégica.
​Si se aprueba, el ítem de PPM puede disparar automáticamente la creación de objetos en IM y/o PS.
​2. Aprobación Financiera y Presupuesto (SAP IM):
​El ítem de PPM se vincula a una Posición del Programa de Inversiones en IM (a veces pasando primero por una Medida / Solicitud de Inversión en IM para su aprobación formal).
​La dirección asigna el presupuesto anual o plurianual en IM.
​3. Ejecución Detallada (SAP PS):
​Al aprobarse la inversión, se crea (o vincula) una Definición de Proyecto y sus Elementos PEP en PS.
​El presupuesto aprobado en IM se transfiere hacia abajo (Top-Down) al Elemento PEP correspondiente en PS.
​En PS se ejecutan las compras (MM), imputaciones de horas (CATS/HR), consumos y controles de disponibilidad presupuestaria (AVAC).
​4. Retroalimentación y Cierre (PS \rightarrow IM \rightarrow PPM):
​Hacia IM: Los costos planificados, comprometidos y reales registrados en PS suben (Bottom-Up) a las posiciones del programa en IM para el control presupuestario consolidado de la empresa. Al cierre, PS liquida los costos hacia Activos Fijos en Curso (AuC) y luego a Activos Fijos definitivos.
​Hacia PPM: Los avances físicos (fechas, hitos, porcentajes de avance) y financieros (costos reales y presupuestos) de PS se sincronizan con el proyecto/ítem de PPM para que los ejecutivos visualicen el estado real del portafolio en sus dashboards.

País de Asignación: México

Tipo de Proyecto: Implementación

Inicio del Proyecto: 2026-11-30

Duración del Proyecto: 6 meses

Modalidad de Trabajo: Remoto

Idioma: Español

jobs.description:
Job Title: Ingénieur(e) principal(e), logiciels et plateformes, équipe Accélérateur

Job Location: Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Ingénieur(e) principal(e), logiciels et plateformes, équipe Accélérateur

Lieu : Télétravail, Canada (chevauchement requis avec les fuseaux horaires américains : heures principales d’environ 8 h à 17 h, HE [à confirmer])

Profil du poste : Contributeur individuel principal (portée et autonomie de niveau staff)

Résumé du poste

IQVIA recherche un(e) ingénieur(e) principal(e), logiciels et plateformes, pour faire évoluer des prototypes et des preuves de concept vers des solutions alpha et bêta déployables, en s’appuyant sur des plateformes internes et externes, notamment l’usine logicielle interne d’IQVIA lorsque celle-ci convient. Notre équipe Accélérateur utilise le développement assisté par l’IA pour concevoir et évaluer rapidement de nouveaux concepts. Ce poste constitue la première capacité dédiée d’ingénierie logicielle et de plateforme de l’équipe : vous ferez progresser les concepts les plus prometteurs vers des projets pilotes chez les clients, puis vers des produits commerciaux.

C’est l’occasion de façonner la manière dont un chef de file mondial des données et de l’analytique en santé commercialise des produits fondés sur l’IA. Vous serez responsable des fondations sur lesquelles repose chaque nouveau projet et verrez votre travail atteindre de véritables utilisateurs.

La personne titulaire établira également le parcours de développement par défaut de l’équipe, en partant de l’usine logicielle lorsqu’elle convient et en s’en écartant de façon délibérée lorsqu’elle ne convient pas : normes, modèles et garde-fous sur lesquels repose chaque nouveau projet afin de réduire les reprises à l’étape du prototypage. Ainsi, le travail assisté par l’IA commence sur une base sécurisée et maintenable et progresse de la preuve de concept aux versions alpha et bêta, puis au produit, sans réingénierie majeure.

Il s’agit d’un rôle pratique qui couvre le développement d’applications et l’ingénierie de plateforme. Il offre une grande autonomie et une collaboration étroite avec les clients et les parties prenantes de l’entreprise.

À quoi ressemble la réussite au cours de la première année

Dans les 90 premiers jours : le parcours de développement par défaut (modèles de dépôts et de pipelines, modules d’infrastructure en tant que code, authentification, gestion des secrets, journalisation, observabilité et analyse de sécurité) est opérationnel et utilisé par tous les nouveaux projets de l’équipe Accélérateur.

Dans les 6 premiers mois : des environnements reproductibles de développement, alpha et bêta fonctionnent sur AWS au moyen de GitLab CI/CD; la première soumission à une revue d’architecture est terminée et consignée sous forme de modèle réutilisable.

Dans les 12 premiers mois : deux prototypes ont été amenés à l’étape de projet pilote chez un client; des critères documentés encadrent le passage d’un concept d’une étape à la suivante; les trousses de démarrage et guides opérationnels ont été améliorés à partir de chaque mandat.

À propos de l’équipe

L’équipe Accélérateur crée des produits pour les processus réglementaires, cliniques, de qualité et commerciaux. Vous serez la première personne de l’équipe entièrement consacrée à l’ingénierie de plateforme et à la transformation de prototypes en produits, aux côtés d’une personne responsable de la création de produits (non ingénieure, mais expérimentée en programmation assistée par l’IA fondée sur des spécifications et des tests) et d’un(e) ingénieur(e) en IA appliquée. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec des chercheurs, des stratèges et des spécialistes des domaines concernés. L’équipe relève de la direction technologique et contribue directement à définir la prestation des solutions, conformément aux processus établis de l’entreprise. Les décisions techniques vous appartiendront en grande partie, dans le respect des exigences d’architecture d’entreprise, de sécurité, de gestion des changements et de mise en production. Vous contribuerez aussi à adapter ces processus aux projets rapides de l’équipe Accélérateur.

Principales responsabilités

Présentées par ordre de priorité. Durant la première année, le parcours de développement par défaut et la transformation des prototypes en produits seront les plus importants.

Parcours de développement par défaut : Définir et maintenir le point de départ standard des nouveaux projets (adaptable aux langages et cadres technologiques de chaque projet), en utilisant l’usine logicielle d’IQVIA lorsqu’elle convient et en documentant les écarts justifiés lorsqu’elle ne convient pas. Cela comprend les modèles de dépôts et de pipelines, les modules d’infrastructure en tant que code ainsi que l’authentification, la gestion des secrets, la journalisation et l’observabilité intégrées. Établir des conventions, garde-fous et pratiques de révision qui assurent la sécurité du code généré par l’IA, sa mise à l’essai et sa conformité aux normes d’ingénierie, notamment l’analyse statique, la vérification des types, les structures de tests et l’analyse de sécurité.

Collaboration avec l’usine logicielle : Évaluer les modèles et services prescriptifs de l’usine logicielle en fonction des besoins de chaque projet. Les utiliser lorsqu’ils conviennent; sinon, présenter et défendre des solutions de rechange auprès de l’équipe plateforme et des responsables des revues d’architecture, avec des preuves relatives aux coûts, aux risques et à la maintenabilité, et réintégrer les actifs de l’équipe Accélérateur lorsque cela est utile.

Transformation des prototypes en produits : Évaluer le code des prototypes pour déterminer ce qui doit être conservé, remanié ou remplacé, et le faire évoluer vers des applications alpha et bêta déployables, couvrant les couches frontales, dorsales, API et d’intégration. Mettre en œuvre des tests et contrôles de qualité adaptés à chaque stade de maturité.

Ingénierie de plateforme : Mettre en place des environnements reproductibles de développement, alpha et bêta sur AWS, à l’aide de l’infrastructure en tant que code, de GitLab CI/CD et de la conteneurisation, en s’appuyant sur les services de l’usine logicielle lorsqu’ils conviennent. Adapter l’approche à Azure, Google Cloud ou aux environnements hébergés par les clients lorsque le projet l’exige.

Préparation aux exigences de l’entreprise : Harmoniser les solutions avec l’infrastructure, les modèles de référence et les normes d’ingénierie de l’entreprise, et négocier des exceptions documentées lorsque l’usine logicielle ne convient pas. Intégrer la livraison de l’équipe aux processus existants de cycle de développement logiciel, de sécurité, de gestion des changements et de mise en production. Préparer les soumissions aux revues d’architecture et élaborer des modèles réutilisables pour les revues ultérieures.

Actifs réutilisables : Développer des composants réutilisables, des trousses de démarrage et des guides opérationnels, et améliorer le parcours de développement par défaut selon les leçons tirées de chaque mandat.

Validation auprès des clients : Livrer des solutions fonctionnelles pour les projets pilotes, les demandes de propositions et les occasions commerciales stratégiques, puis les améliorer selon les commentaires des clients et des parties prenantes.

Jugement fondé sur les risques : Appliquer une rigueur d’ingénierie proportionnelle aux risques et au stade de maturité, et conseiller sur les conditions de passage de chaque concept à l’étape suivante (par exemple, décider s’il faut remanier ou reconstruire un prototype avant un projet pilote chez un client).

Soutien opérationnel : Soutenir les projets pilotes et les environnements alpha et bêta, avec des attentes de disponibilité sur appel et de soutien adaptées à chaque stade de maturité.

Qualifications requises

Au moins 5 ans d’expérience professionnelle en génie logiciel, notamment dans la création et le déploiement d’applications infonuagiques

Expérience démontrée dans l’évolution de logiciels, du prototype au projet pilote ou au déploiement en production

Solides compétences en développement full stack, y compris la capacité d’évaluer, de remanier et d’étendre de façon autonome des bases de code existantes dans divers langages et cadres technologiques

Expérience avec AWS (Azure ou Google Cloud constitue un atout), la conception de pipelines CI/CD (GitLab CI/CD fortement privilégié), l’infrastructure en tant que code (Terraform ou CloudFormation), les flux de travail Git, Docker et l’intégration d’API REST

Expérience pratique des outils de développement assisté par l’IA (p. ex., Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) et compréhension éclairée de la gouvernance de la qualité et de la sécurité du code généré par l’IA

Connaissance pratique de la sécurité infonuagique, de l’identité, de l’authentification, de l’autorisation et de la gestion des secrets

Expérience de création de modèles de projets réutilisables, de parcours de référence ou de plateformes internes pour développeurs adoptés par d’autres ingénieurs, et jugement quant au moment où suivre, étendre ou contourner une plateforme prescriptive existante

Expérience de l’intégration de grands modèles de langage, d’agents d’IA ou d’API de modèles dans des applications

Capacité de remettre en question de manière constructive et factuelle les décisions de plateforme et d’architecture, et d’influencer les équipes plateforme et d’entreprise sans autorité hiérarchique directe

Bon jugement pour équilibrer rapidité, qualité, sécurité et évolutivité, et capacité de prendre des décisions techniques de manière autonome, notamment en expliquant comment vous avez décidé de conserver, remanier ou reconstruire des éléments d’un prototype antérieur

Qualifications souhaitées

Maîtrise de Python et de TypeScript/React, et aisance avec d’autres langages et cadres technologiques (par exemple Java, .NET ou Node.js) selon les projets

Expérience avec Kubernetes

Connaissance des passerelles API comme Kong, des bases de données NoSQL comme DynamoDB, ainsi que des cadres d’applications de grands modèles de langage et des outils d’observabilité comme LangChain et LangSmith

Expérience avec des outils d’observabilité comme CloudWatch ou Datadog

Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés comme les soins de santé, les sciences de la vie, les technologies médicales ou les services financiers, notamment les BPF/BPL (GxP), la validation des systèmes informatisés (CSV/CSA) ou les comités de revue d’architecture

Expérience de mise en œuvre de tests automatisés liés aux exigences dans les pipelines CI

Expérience dans une jeune entreprise, un incubateur ou un environnement de produits en phase de démarrage

Environnement technologique

Notre pile technologique varie selon le projet, le client et le prototype transformé en produit. Vous établirez un parcours par défaut cohérent tout en vous adaptant aux outils requis par chaque concept. Voici ce à quoi vous pouvez vous attendre :

Plateforme interne : Usine logicielle d’IQVIA (modèles et services prescriptifs, actuellement fondés sur Kong, AWS, DynamoDB et LangChain/LangSmith) utilisée par défaut lorsqu’elle convient, avec des exceptions documentées dans les autres cas

Infonuagique : AWS (principal); Azure ou Google Cloud selon les besoins du client ou du projet

CI/CD : GitLab CI/CD

Infrastructure en tant que code : Terraform ou CloudFormation

Conteneurs : Docker, Kubernetes

Langages : Python et TypeScript/React le plus souvent; autres langages et cadres selon le prototype transformé en produit

Observabilité : CloudWatch, Datadog ou équivalent

Développement assisté par l’IA : Claude Code, Cursor, Codex ou outils semblables

Plateformes d’agents et outils habilitants : Écosystème Microsoft; Copilot Studio, Foundry, PowerApps, PowerAutomate, MCP, A2A, A2UI (connaissance utile, mais non requise)

Senior Software & Platform Engineer, Accelerator

Location: Remote, Canada (U.S. time-zone overlap required: core hours roughly 8:00 am–5:00 pm ET [confirm])

Employment Profile: Senior Individual Contributor (staff-level scope and autonomy)

Role Summary

IQVIA is seeking a Senior Software & Platform Engineer to mature prototypes and proofs of concept into deployable alpha and beta solutions, leveraging both internal platforms and external ones, including IQVIA's internal software factory where it fits. Our accelerator team uses AI-assisted development to build and evaluate new concepts rapidly. This role is the team's founding engineering and platform capability: you will advance the most promising concepts to client pilots and, ultimately, to commercial products.

This is an opportunity to shape how a global leader in healthcare data and analytics ships AI-enabled products. You will own the foundation every new project is built on and see your work reach real users.

The engineer will also establish the team's default development path, starting from the software factory where it fits and diverging deliberately where it does not: the standards, templates, and guardrails on which every new project is built in order to reduce rework at the prototyping stage. This ensures that AI-assisted work begins on a secure, maintainable foundation and progresses from proof of concept to alpha, beta, and product without substantial re-engineering.

This is a hands-on role spanning application development and platform engineering. It offers significant autonomy and close engagement with clients and business stakeholders.

What Success Looks Like in the First Year

  • Within 90 days: the default development path (repository and pipeline templates, Infrastructure as Code modules, authentication, secrets management, logging, observability, and security scanning) is live and used by all new accelerator projects.
  • Within 6 months: repeatable development, alpha, and beta environments are running on AWS through GitLab CI/CD, and the first architecture review submission is complete and captured as a reusable template.
  • Within 12 months: two prototypes have been taken to client pilot, documented criteria exist for advancing a concept from one stage to the next, and starter kits and runbooks have been refined from each engagement.

About the Team

The accelerator team builds products for Regulatory, Clinical, Quality, and Commercial workflows. The engineer will be the team's first dedicated platform and productization engineer, working alongside a product builder (non-engineer, but experienced in spec-driven and test-driven AI-assisted coding) and an applied AI engineer, in close partnership with researchers, strategists, and domain subject-matter experts. The team reports to technology leadership and contributes directly to defining how solutions are delivered, in alignment with established enterprise processes. Technical decisions are largely yours to make, within enterprise architecture, security, change, and release requirements, and part of the job is helping shape how those processes work for fast-moving accelerator projects.

Key Responsibilities

Listed in priority order. In year one, the default development path and prototype productization carry the most weight.

  • Default development path: Define and maintain the standard starting point for new projects (adaptable to the languages and frameworks each project uses), starting from the IQVIA software factory where it fits and documenting justified deviations where it does not, including repository and pipeline templates, Infrastructure as Code modules, and built-in authentication, secrets management, logging, and observability. Establish conventions, guardrails, and review practices that keep AI-generated code secure, tested, and consistent with engineering standards, including linting, type checking, test scaffolding, and security scanning.
  • Software factory partnership: Assess the software factory's opinionated templates and services against each project's needs. Use them where they fit; where they do not, make and defend the case for alternatives, with evidence on cost, risk, and maintainability, to the platform team and architecture reviewers, and contribute accelerator assets back where useful.
  • Prototype productization: Evaluate prototype code to determine what should be retained, refactored, or replaced, and evolve it into deployable alpha and beta applications across front-end, back-end, API, and integration layers. Implement testing and quality controls appropriate to each stage of maturity.
  • Platform engineering: Establish repeatable development, alpha, and beta environments on AWS using Infrastructure as Code, GitLab CI/CD, and containerization, building on software factory services where they fit, and adapt the approach to Azure, Google Cloud, or client-hosted environments when a project requires it.
  • Enterprise readiness: Align solutions with company infrastructure, reference patterns, and enterprise engineering standards, and negotiate documented exceptions where the software factory does not fit. Integrate team delivery with existing SDLC, security, change, and release processes. Prepare architecture review submissions and develop reusable templates for subsequent reviews.
  • Reusable assets: Develop reusable components, starter kits, and runbooks, and refine the default development path based on lessons learned from each engagement.
  • Client validation: Deliver working solutions for client pilots, RFPs, and strategic business opportunities, and iterate based on client and stakeholder feedback.
  • Risk-based judgment: Apply engineering rigor proportionate to risk and stage of maturity, and advise on the requirements for advancing each concept to its next stage (for example, deciding whether a prototype is refactored or rebuilt before a client pilot).
  • Operational support: Support pilots and alpha and beta environments, with on-call and support expectations scaled to each stage of maturity.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience building and deploying cloud applications
  • Demonstrated experience advancing software from prototype to pilot or production deployment
  • Strong full-stack engineering skills, including the ability to independently assess, refactor, and extend existing codebases written in a range of languages and frameworks
  • Experience with AWS (experience with Azure or Google Cloud is a plus), CI/CD pipeline design (GitLab CI/CD strongly preferred), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform or CloudFormation), Git-based workflows, Docker, and REST API integration
  • Practical experience with AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and an informed perspective on governing the quality and security of AI-generated code
  • Working knowledge of cloud security, identity, authentication, authorization, and secrets management
  • Experience building reusable project templates, golden paths, or internal developer platforms that other engineers adopted, and judgment about when to follow, extend, or deviate from an existing opinionated platform
  • Experience integrating large language models, AI agents, or model APIs into applications
  • Ability to push back constructively and with evidence on platform and architecture decisions, and to influence platform and enterprise teams without direct authority
  • Sound judgment in balancing speed, quality, security, and scalability, and the ability to make technical decisions independently, including how you decided what to keep, refactor, or rebuild in a past prototype

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proficiency in Python and TypeScript/React, and comfort working in other languages and frameworks (for example Java, .NET, or Node.js) as projects require
  • Experience with Kubernetes
  • Familiarity with API gateways such as Kong, NoSQL data stores such as DynamoDB, and LLM application frameworks and observability tools such as LangChain and LangSmith
  • Experience with observability tools such as CloudWatch or Datadog
  • Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, life sciences, medical technology, or financial services, including GxP, CSV/CSA, or architecture review boards
  • Experience implementing automated tests traced to requirements within CI pipelines
  • Experience in startup, incubator, or early-stage product environments

Technology Environment

Our stack varies by project, client, and the prototype being productized. You will establish a consistent default path while adapting to the tools each concept requires. Expect the following:

About Widewail

Widewail is a Burlington, Vermont-based technology company helping businesses better understand their customers, strengthen their online reputation, and make more informed business decisions.

Our platform brings together customer feedback, operational data, and artificial intelligence to help businesses understand what's driving customer satisfaction, identify opportunities for improvement, and deliver better customer experiences. From automating customer engagement and managing online reviews to competitive benchmarking and actionable customer intelligence, we're helping businesses turn customer feedback into a competitive advantage.

We're solving interesting technical challenges at the intersection of data engineering, artificial intelligence, automation, and cloud-native software development. We're continually evolving our platform, expanding our capabilities, and finding new ways to deliver meaningful value to our customers.

We're a collaborative, pragmatic team that values curiosity, ownership, thoughtful decision-making, and continuous improvement. We care about what we build, how we build it, and the impact it has on the businesses and people who rely on us.

Hiring in the following states: Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Maine, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Texas, Vermont.

Compensation and benefits
  • $80,000–$125,000 annually, depending on experience.
  • Widewail benefits include:
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage, with HSA, FSA, and dependent care account options
  • Company-funded Lifestyle Spending Account
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Combined time off and paid holidays
  • Remote-first working environment
Who we’re looking for

At Widewail, we're building technology that helps businesses better understand their customers, improve their reputation, and turn customer feedback into meaningful insights. We're looking for a Software Engineer II to help us build and improve the systems that make that possible.

This is a hands-on role where you'll join a collaborative engineering team, working primarily with Java, Spring Boot, and Python to develop backend services, APIs, and integrations that power our platform. You'll work closely with other engineers and Product and Data Science stakeholders, contributing to technical decisions and taking ownership of well-scoped work through delivery and production support.

If you're a curious, pragmatic engineer who enjoys solving problems, values collaboration, and takes pride in building reliable software, this might be a good fit.

What you’ll do
  • Build, test, and maintain backend applications and services using Java, Spring Boot, Kotlin, and Python.
  • Develop APIs, integrations, and data processing workflows that support our products and customer-facing capabilities.
  • Break down and deliver well-scoped features and improvements, with guidance from senior engineers on more complex technical decisions.
  • Contribute to reliable applications using AWS, relational databases, and cloud-native technologies.
  • Work with third-party APIs and external data providers to support reliable data exchange and processing.
  • Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to understand requirements, clarify questions, and deliver practical solutions.
  • Consider performance, security, maintainability, and simplicity when implementing solutions.
  • Write automated tests and use logging, metrics, and monitoring to understand the behavior of your changes.
  • Investigate and resolve defects and production issues, escalating risks and blockers appropriately.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and planning, sharing progress and giving constructive feedback.
Who you are
  • Experience building and maintaining production backend applications, ideally in a SaaS or technology environment.
  • Proficient in Java, Python, or a comparable backend programming language, and interested in working across Java and Python.
  • Experience with Spring Boot or a similar backend application framework is preferred, but not required.
  • Familiar with AWS or comparable cloud-native technologies and interested in deepening your experience.
  • Working knowledge of relational databases, SQL, REST APIs, and asynchronous or event-driven systems.
  • Comfortable with Git-based development, automated testing, CI/CD, and basic production troubleshooting.
  • Able to break down tasks, estimate work, and deliver quality changes with limited day-to-day supervision.
  • Pragmatic in your approach: you look for opportunities to ship useful improvements early and keep changes manageable.
  • Take ownership of your work, communicate progress and blockers, and seek input when needed.
  • Collaborative and approachable, you value feedback, assume positive intent, and build productive working relationships.
  • Curious and self-directed, with a willingness to learn new technologies and improve your engineering practices.
  • Bonus: experience with infrastructure as code, data pipelines, third-party integrations, observability, or AI-assisted development tools.
Why this role matters

Our platform depends on reliable backend services, thoughtful integrations, and the ability to turn complex data into useful customer experiences. This role will help us improve our core applications, deliver new capabilities, and maintain the quality and reliability of the systems our customers depend on.

You'll have the opportunity to grow your skills, take meaningful ownership of your work, and contribute to a team focused on building better software and delivering value to customers consistently.

jobs.excerpt: Description MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.
jobs.description:
Description

MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi’s technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality.

As our Product Manager for Insurance, you’ll own an entirely new product line: bringing insurance payments to a platform that today runs almost entirely on self-pay. You’ll build eligibility, prior authorization, and claims into a business already handling ~18,000 visits a month, a genuine zero-to-one effort that opens a new revenue stream for the company.You’ll own the “coverage truth” (eligibility and benefits, the payer → plan → coverage data model, and cost-share), the economics of the insurance model, prior authorization flows, and the path from visit to claim to payment. You’ll work at the intersection of clinical, finance, engineering, and legal, partnering with a cross-functional pod of engineers and QA that will grow as the line scales.

Why this role:

  • Zero-to-one ownership. You’re standing up an entire insurance product line from scratch inside a profitable, working telehealth business
  • Measured impact. Your work opens a new revenue stream, and success is measured in insured visits paid at the expected rate, denial rate, and time to cash, not features shipped.
  • Breadth and real influence. You’ll operate across clinical, finance, product, and engineering, owning the systems a dozen stakeholders depend on and driving the decisions that unblock launch.

Responsibilities

  • Own insurance as a product line. The insurance team is the centre of product decisions for everything insurance touches.
  • Launch insurance end to end. Map how insurance should work at MEDvidi, prototype it, and validate it against real cases with revenue-cycle staff, coordinators and patients. Take every decision blocking launch to the people who own it, with a recommendation and a deadline, and coordinate the launch across teams and vendors.
  • Coverage. Eligibility and benefits checks, the payer → plan → coverage data model, and cost-share (copay, deductible, coinsurance), so every booking gets a correct answer on coverage and on what the patient owes before the visit.
  • Patient money. Estimates before the visit, collecting copay and deductible, balances after the payer adjudicates, statements, superbills for out-of-network patients, and the rules for when an insured patient can still pay cash.
  • Prior authorisation. From prescription to medication in hand, plus visit authorisations where payers require them.
  • Visit to claim to payment. With the team, build the full revenue-cycle loop: claims, clearinghouse, remittance, denials and appeals.

This role is not for you if:

  • You want a defined roadmap and clean requirements handed to you: here, the requirements don’t exist yet, and you build them from knowledge scattered across teams and vendors.
  • You think of the job as shipping features as specified, rather than owning a business outcome you can measure in money.
  • You wait for authority before you act, or you’re uncomfortable driving and escalating decisions with people who don’t report to you.

Requirements

  • 6+ years senior-level product management experience, including ownership of complex, systems-heavy products where a change in one place ripples into many others under high uncertainty.
  • A track record of turning stakeholder requests and feature “wants” into the real business problem worth solving, cutting what isn’t needed and reframing what is.
  • An ownership mindset: you build alignment across teams through context and arguments, not authority; come with a clear proposal (“here’s how I suggest this works”); and when a decision stalls, bring options and a recommendation to the people who need to weigh in, rather than waiting for someone else to decide.
  • Outcome-driven to the core: you measure yourself in business results: denial rate, time to cash and you dig into the data yourself to find where value leaks.
  • Advanced English (C1+) your primary stakeholders are US-based and fluent Russian.
  • Remote, with working hours that overlap the team in CET and some overlap with US-based stakeholders.

Would be a plus:

  • Hands-on familiarity with US health insurance and the revenue cycle: eligibility and benefits, prior authorization, claims, denials, and reimbursement.
  • AI as a working tool: you use tools like Claude and Cursor to prototype and iterate fast, and you know where AI should and shouldn’t be applied.
  • Experience building something zero-to-one in a regulated environment (HIPAA or similar).

What we offer

  • High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space.
  • Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package.
  • Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model.
  • Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation.
  • Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply.
  • Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days.
  • Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events.

Ready to make an impact? Send us your profile, let’s build something meaningful together.

MEDvidi is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and contractors. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

This role is focused on advancing NOAA's operational flood mapping capabilities that support national water prediction services. The position will contribute directly to the development of prototype and production-ready 1D/2D hydraulic modeling frameworks to support the continued expansion of high-fidelity flood inundation mapping forecasts.

The successful candidate will work across hydraulic engineering, hydrologic science, geospatial programming, and research-to-operations activities to develop, validate, and operationalize flood mapping products using 1D/2D hydraulic models.   • Develop, calibrate, validate, and evaluate one-dimensional and two-dimensional hydraulic models supporting operational flood inundation mapping.
  • Generate flood extents, flood depths, rating relationships, and flood mapping libraries using hydraulic models/tools (e.g. HEC-RAS).
  • Integrate terrain, bathymetry, hydrofabric, stream network, land-surface, and observational datasets into hydraulic modeling workflows.
  • Evaluate model performance against benchmark flood extents, high-water marks, surveyed water surfaces, and other authoritative observations.
  • Develop and improve methodologies that increase flood mapping accuracy while maintaining operational scalability and computational efficiency.
  • Design and automate workflows for model setup, mesh generation, calibration, execution, quality control, and production of flood mapping products.

About the Role

We are hiring a hands-on Senior Solution Architect to lead architecture, presales, forward deployed engineering (FDE), and delivery across modern application platforms spanning cloud-native, on-premises, and hybrid environments.

This role operates flexibly across presales, delivery, or both within a client engagement, shaping solutions, contributing to bids, and ensuring execution aligned with business outcomes.

You will work directly with clients to understand complex business and technical challenges, translate ambiguous requirements into practical solutions, and actively participate in engineering and implementation.

This role is suited for architects who can independently shape, win, build, and deliver complex modern application solutions.

You will work with highly technical clients and strong offshore engineering teams, where your value is measured by the depth of your technical expertise, clarity of solution structuring, consulting, storytelling, and ability to influence outcomes from day one.

What You Will Do

  • Define end-to-end architectures using microservices, event-driven architecture, and distributed system patterns.
  • Apply architecture frameworks, design patterns, and well-architected principles across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments.
  • Architect and deliver high-volume, low-latency, mission-critical enterprise platforms, ensuring scalability, resilience, security, and performance.
  • Drive application modernization initiatives, including Monolith to Microservices, Batch to Event-driven, and Legacy to Cloud-native / Cloud-ready architectures.
  • Architect event-driven systems using Kafka, messaging, and streaming technologies.
  • Solve complex distributed system challenges, including failure handling, retries, consistency, scalability, and latency.

  • Act as a trusted technical advisor to clients, leading discovery workshops, architecture discussions, solution presentations, and technical deep-dive sessions.
  • Contribute directly to RFP/RFI responses, technical proposals, effort estimation, implementation strategies, and risk assessments.
  • Articulate business value, architectural trade-offs, technical feasibility, and expected business outcomes through compelling solution storytelling.
  • Navigate enterprise complexity and collaborate with internal teams to identify relevant success stories, benchmarks, modernization patterns, and reusable capabilities.
  • Work directly with client business and engineering teams to understand real-world challenges, technical constraints, and operational requirements.
  • Translate complex and ambiguous business requirements into actionable, scalable, and production-ready solutions.
  • Actively contribute to software engineering, including writing code, building integrations, reviewing code, debugging, and resolving complex technical issues.
  • Rapidly develop and iterate on demos, POCs, and MVPs using technologies such as Spring Boot, Quarkus, REST/gRPC, Java, and .NET to validate solutions, support proposals, and accelerate client adoption.
  • Take end-to-end technical ownership from problem discovery and solution design through implementation, production deployment, and adoption.
  • Collaborate with strong offshore engineering teams through deep technical guidance and direct contributions to solution proposals, architecture artefacts, and implementation, rather than merely supervising delivery.
  • Remove technical implementation blockers and adapt solutions to fit existing enterprise technology ecosystems.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI, automation, and emerging technologies to address client challenges.
  • Translate client implementation experiences into reusable engineering accelerators, reference architectures, and solution patterns.
  • Thrive in fast-paced, dynamic, and highly technical client-facing environments.
  • Be self-driven, proactive, and outcome-focused, with the ability to deliver independently without repeated follow-ups.
  • Influence technical and business stakeholders through engineering credibility, consulting capabilities, and effective communication.

  • Strong expertise in distributed systems, API design, REST/gRPC, messaging, and event-streaming technologies such as Kafka.
  • Experience in application modernization and architecture across cloud-native, on-premises, and hybrid environments.
  • Proven experience across presales, technical solutioning, consulting, and enterprise delivery.
  • Demonstrated ability to rapidly translate business problems into functional prototypes, MVPs, or production-ready solutions.
  • Experience with containerization, CI/CD, DevOps, observability, and performance engineering.
  • Ability to operate independently in complex client environments and collaborate effectively with distributed and offshore engineering teams.
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management, presentation, and technical storytelling skills.

Good to Have

jobs.description:
Remote (US-based) · Freelance, project-based · Paid by project, per word, or by article length, DOE

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

About Red Door Collaborative

Red Door Collaborative is a creative agency serving enterprise tech organizations and SMBs with visual design, content, motion, and video work. We're a small, human-centered team: highly collaborative, quietly intense, and genuinely good at what we do. We're also evolving. AI is reshaping our industry, and we're leaning into it as a tool that enhances our work rather than replaces the people doing it.

We're rooted in SoCal and the PNW, but we're a fully remote team of creatives. We work Pacific hours and meet in person rarely. This is a real remote role, not a "remote for now" situation. This role requires someone who can take a written brief and a few subject-matter calls, then deliver polished long-form drafts on schedule, with clear communication through Microsoft Teams along the way.

About the Role

We're looking for a freelance long-form writer to join our bench of individual collaborators. Our clients sell sophisticated cloud, data, and AI products. Your job is to make those products make sense to the people buying them, in eBooks, long-form articles, and blog posts written in plain, engaging language.

This isn't developer documentation. It's marketing writing that takes something complex and makes it clear and approachable. Work comes in by assignment as projects need it. Our Sr. Creative Strategist, Content and Marketing briefs and reviews the work.

What You'll Do

  • Long-form writing: Write eBooks, long-form articles, and blog posts from a creative brief, from outline through final draft.
  • Making complex things clear: Turn product information, technical source material, and subject-matter-expert interviews into copy a non-technical reader can follow and enjoy.
  • Voice and accuracy: Write in each client's brand voice while keeping every technical claim accurate.
  • Revisions: Take feedback from our team and client reviewers and turn revisions quickly and cleanly.

Who You Are

  • Experience: You have 5+ years of experience writing long-form marketing content for technology companies, or for an agency with technology clients.
  • Plain-language skill: Your samples show complex technical topics explained in a way everyday business readers understand.
  • Fast research: You can learn a new product quickly from source material and a short subject-matter-expert call.
  • Independence: You manage your own schedule and deliver on agreed deadlines without needing reminders.
  • AI-forward: Red Door is an AI-forward agency. You use AI tools in your research and writing workflow, you look for new ways to make them useful, and you keep the final voice human.

Before You Apply

Consider the following before applying:

  • If you're looking for steady, full-time hours rather than project-based work…
  • If your writing experience is mostly technical documentation rather than marketing…
  • If you're more comfortable writing for experts than explaining things to everyone else…

Then this probably isn't the right role for you.

To Apply

In your cover letter, tell us about the most complicated thing you've ever had to explain in writing and how you made it click for your reader. Include links to 2 to 3 long-form samples. We'd rather hear your honest take than a polished answer.

During the process, we may ask you to complete a short writing exercise. Finalists will be asked to provide references from creatives they've worked with directly.

Compensation

This is a freelance, project-based engagement, not employment. Depending on the assignment, we pay a flat project rate, a per-word rate, or a rate based on article length. Rates are agreed in writing before work starts and reflect the scope of the work and your experience. Individual collaborators are not eligible for employee benefits.

Equal Opportunity

Red Door Collaborative is committed to building an inclusive team where everyone is valued and respected. We don't discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status. We don't just welcome diverse perspectives; we actively seek them out. People from different cultures and experiences, solving problems together, is how we do our best work.

Prime Pensions, Inc. is a well-established retirement plan administration and actuarial firm specializing in 401(k), profit sharing, defined benefit, and other qualified retirement plans for employers across the United States.

Since 1975, Prime Pensions has provided customized retirement plan solutions with an emphasis on technical expertise, accuracy, and personalized service. Our team supports a wide variety of plan designs and investment arrangements while maintaining comprehensive oversight and quality standards throughout the administration process.

Prime Pensions has been recognized as a leading defined contribution plan administrator and as one of NJBIZ's Best Places to Work in New Jersey.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Senior Retirement Plan Administrator is responsible for the ongoing administration, compliance, and client service of qualified retirement plans, including 401(k), Profit Sharing, and Cash Balance plans. This position independently manages assigned retirement plans, performs compliance testing and contribution calculations, maintains accurate plan records, and ensures adherence to applicable regulatory requirements.

The ideal candidate has at least five (5) years of retirement plan administration experience, strong technical and analytical skills, and the ability to independently manage assigned plans while providing exceptional service to clients and financial professionals.

This role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Retirement Plan Administration & Compliance

  • Perform ongoing administration and annual compliance work for qualified retirement plans, including 401(k), Profit Sharing, and Cash Balance plans.
  • Independently manage assigned retirement plans, ensuring accurate and timely completion of administrative responsibilities.
  • Review and interpret plan documents to determine applicable administrative provisions and ensure plans are administered in accordance with plan terms.
  • Determine participant eligibility, compensation, service, and vesting in accordance with plan provisions.
  • Perform annual compliance testing, including ADP/ACP nondiscrimination testing, coverage testing, and Top-Heavy testing.
  • Determine Highly Compensated Employee (HCE) and Key Employee status.
  • Calculate annual employer contributions, including Profit Sharing, Safe Harbor, and other applicable contribution allocations.
  • Assist with Cash Balance plan administration and coordinate applicable actuarial calculations and funding requirements with the actuarial team.
  • Review participant data and plan records to identify discrepancies, missing information, or potential compliance issues.
  • Research administrative and compliance questions and recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Identify potential compliance failures and assist with determining and implementing appropriate correction methods.
  • Maintain accurate and complete plan records and supporting documentation.

Client Service & Consulting Support

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for assigned clients regarding retirement plan administration and compliance matters.
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships with clients, financial advisors, accountants, and other financial professionals.
  • Respond to client inquiries and provide clear, accurate, and timely information regarding plan administration, contribution calculations, and compliance requirements.
  • Assist clients with understanding applicable plan provisions, administrative requirements, and regulatory deadlines.
  • Identify client needs and assist with retirement plan design recommendations and potential plan enhancements.
  • Support annual plan reviews by preparing relevant compliance information, contribution calculations, and administrative summaries.
  • Troubleshoot client issues and coordinate with internal departments to ensure timely and effective resolution.
  • Communicate complex retirement plan information in a clear and professional manner.
  • Escalate complex technical or compliance matters to the appropriate internal resources when necessary.

Annual Reporting & Regulatory Compliance

  • Prepare and review applicable annual retirement plan reporting information and supporting documentation.
  • Assist with the preparation and filing of Form 5500 and related schedules, as applicable.
  • Review plan financial information, participant census data, and contribution records for accuracy and completeness.
  • Monitor applicable regulatory deadlines and ensure assigned administrative work is completed within established timeframes.
  • Coordinate with internal trust accounting, actuarial, and compliance teams to obtain necessary information for annual reporting.
  • Stay informed of regulatory changes affecting qualified retirement plans and apply updated requirements to assigned administrative responsibilities.
  • Assist with plan amendments, restatements, and other administrative updates as required.

Workflow, Systems & Quality Management

  • Manage assigned retirement plan administration workflow to ensure work is completed accurately and within established deadlines.
  • Maintain accurate and timely records of completed and outstanding work within Company workflow, time-tracking, and administration systems, including WIP, Time Tracker, and APC Gold.
  • Meet established internal turnaround times, productivity expectations, and quality standards.
  • Review work for accuracy and completeness prior to finalization or delivery.
  • Effectively prioritize multiple plans, client requests, and administrative deadlines, particularly during peak workload periods.
  • Utilize retirement plan administration software and Microsoft Office applications to complete assigned work efficiently.
  • Maintain reliable and satisfactory attendance.

ADDITIONAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Participate in individual and group discussions regarding departmental procedures, workflow, and process improvements.
  • Assist with technical research, special projects, and implementation of regulatory or procedural changes.
  • Collaborate with Consultants, Compliance Administrators, Trust Administrators, and Actuarial team members to support accurate and timely plan administration.
  • Assist with training and mentoring new or less-experienced employees as appropriate.
  • Share technical knowledge and best practices to support continued departmental development.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Experience

  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in retirement plan administration, preferably within a third-party administration (TPA), retirement plan consulting, or related financial services environment.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Mathematics, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant professional experience may be considered.
  • Demonstrated experience independently administering qualified retirement plans, particularly 401(k) and Profit Sharing plans.
  • Strong working knowledge of Defined Contribution retirement plans, including eligibility, vesting, contribution allocations, and compliance testing.
  • Familiarity with Cash Balance and Defined Benefit retirement plans preferred.
  • Experience performing annual compliance testing and contribution calculations.
  • Experience working directly with clients, financial advisors, or other financial professionals preferred.
  • Industry credentials such as QKA, QPA, or other ASPPA/NAPA certifications are a plus.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Strong working knowledge of qualified retirement plan administration and compliance.
  • Working knowledge of ERISA, the Internal Revenue Code, and applicable IRS and Department of Labor regulations.
  • Strong understanding of retirement plan eligibility, vesting, contribution limits, nondiscrimination testing, and annual reporting requirements.
  • Ability to interpret retirement plan documents, technical guidance, and regulatory information.
  • Strong mathematical, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain a high degree of accuracy.
  • Ability to independently manage assigned retirement plans while appropriately escalating complex or unusual matters.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Ability to research administrative and compliance questions and develop accurate, practical solutions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical retirement plan information to clients and other stakeholders.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and a commitment to providing high-quality client service.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with internal departments and external financial professionals.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and Word.
  • Experience with retirement plan administration and compliance software preferred.
  • Ability to work efficiently and accurately in a deadline-driven environment.
  • Ability to meet established productivity, quality, and turnaround expectations.

PHYSICAL / ENVIRONMENTAL CHARACTERISTICS

Work is primarily performed in a professional office or remote work environment and may require:

  • Sitting for prolonged periods while working at a computer.
  • Frequent use of a computer keyboard, mouse, telephone, and other standard office equipment.
  • Periodic standing, walking, reaching, bending, crouching, or kneeling.
  • Occasionally lifting, carrying, pushing, or pulling office materials weighing up to 30 pounds.
  • Visual, hearing, mobility, and manual dexterity sufficient to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • Full-time position with flexible work arrangements, including in-office, hybrid, and remote opportunities.
  • Annual base salary of $85,000–$105,000, based on relevant retirement plan administration experience, technical expertise, industry credentials, and other job-related qualifications.
  • Annual performance reviews and eligibility for salary increases.
  • Bonus opportunities.
  • Company-sponsored benefits available to eligible full-time employees, including:
    • Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
    • Health Savings Account (HSA), subject to eligibility.
    • Life insurance.
    • 401(k) retirement plan with employer contributions.
    • Paid time off.
    • Actuarial examination and professional development support, where applicable.

All benefits are subject to applicable plan terms, eligibility requirements, and Company policies.

WORK LOCATION

This position offers flexible work arrangements, including in-office, hybrid, or fully remote opportunities.

Employees may work from Prime Pensions' Florham Park, New Jersey office, follow an approved hybrid schedule, or work remotely from an approved location within the United States.

All employees are expected to maintain an appropriate work environment and be available during established working hours to support client service, departmental collaboration, and business needs.
